source.title: Howe duality and dichotomy for exceptional theta correspondences
source.authors: Wee Teck Gan and Gordan Savin
readSections: The whole paper (§§1–15 and the references) in arXiv v1, 31 January 2021, 56 pp., the only arXiv version (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.00372v1; SHA-256 8b3b6702909a6a936e5984f46a3c2fbfe629b63db4ba0ae9bd4356286508c6e5; accessed 2026-09-22). Formulas at the recorded misprints were checked on page images.

The published version (Invent. Math. 232 (2023) 1–78; received 9 September 2021, accepted 15 September 2022) is closed access and was not read. Only its abstract, identical to v1's, was compared. The 2023 sequel cites '[GS, §3.5]' for the L-packet discussion that is §3.4 in v1, so the published numbering may differ.

The sequel, Gan–Savin, The local Langlands conjecture for G_2 (arXiv:2209.07346v2; Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023)): §2, its summary of this paper's results, and its citations of this paper, searched for corrections

Review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026): arXiv v1 (same SHA-256 8b3b6702…) and its TeX source read in full again with four checkers, every item checked against it. The published version (Invent. Math. 232 (2023)) is closed access and was not read; the authors' homepages give no copy.

summary: Gan and Savin study three exceptional theta correspondences over a p-adic field. They restrict the minimal representations of E_6^D, E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and E_7 to the dual pairs PD^× × G_2, (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 and G_2 × PGSp_6, D a cubic division algebra. They prove the Howe duality conjecture for all three (Theorem 1.2), and a dichotomy: every irreducible representation of G_2 lifts to exactly one of PD^× and PGSp_6 (Theorem 1.1). They determine the lifts of all non-supercuspidal representations and prove that the correspondences preserve temperedness and discrete series (Theorem 1.3). With no doubling see-saw available, the method is a 'ping-pong with periods'. Chains of containments between periods (the degenerate Fourier coefficients ψ_E of G_2, and Whittaker, Shalika and Fourier–Jacobi periods) close up through a see-saw with Spin_8^E and a Mackey analysis of its degenerate principal series (§§5–6, 11–12). Jacquet-module filtrations of the minimal representations handle the non-tempered and noncuspidal parts (§§13–14). The results are the input to the local Langlands correspondence for G_2 (PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B). Tau Ceti has the split octonions, one library item, and its roadmaps plan the exceptional Lie algebras and the Chevalley groups. Smooth representation tools are planned in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups. Nothing plans minimal representations, exceptional dual pairs or the representation theory of p-adic G_2. Of 87 items, 1 is in the libraries, 2 are planned and 84 are missing. The missing items go to a new roadmap, ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2 (78), with sources for MP.3 (4, classical theta inputs), SR.3 (1) and ML.4 (1, the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4). There are 22 source issues, recorded against arXiv v1: fifteen misprints, one error and six gaps. The error is that §9's 'Weyl-invariant quadratic form' is invariant on cocharacters, not on the characters it is written for. The gaps are unproved computations and cases left to the reader. After the review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23) there are 107 items (1 library, 3 planned, 103 missing) and 52 source issues. E1–E22 are confirmed. In arXiv v1 the proofs of the dichotomy and of Howe duality rest on several steps stated without proof (E10, E12, E13, E20–E22); the review sharpened their reach. It also found a gap in Proposition 10.4 for non-generic τ. It found that the genericity clause of Theorem 8.2(i) and Theorem 8.5(iii) fails for nontempered generic τ, and that §8.1 omits the trivial representation. Whether the published version fills these gaps could not be checked.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 = Theorem 6.1 (theta dichotomy)
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic 0 and π ∈ Irr(G_2(F)). Then π has nonzero theta lift to exactly one of PD^× (D a cubic division F-algebra) or PGSp_6(F).
items.note: Theta lifts are taken in the restriction of the minimal representation of E_6^D, respectively E_7, to the dual pairs PD^× × G_2 and G_2 × PGSp_6. Nontempered and generic π are handled by the Jacquet-module computations and [GS04, Cor. 20]; nongeneric tempered π by the see-saw of §5 and the chain of containments of Lemma 6.4. Review note: Status missing is right: no atlas stage plans exceptional theta correspondences (route 1). Checked against p. 2 and Theorem 6.1, p. 19; F is any p-adic field of characteristic 0 (no restriction on p).

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (Howe duality for the three dual pairs)
items.statement: The Howe duality conjecture holds for the dual pairs PD^× × G_2 ⊂ E_6^D, (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 ⊂ E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and G_2 × PGSp_6 ⊂ E_7: for π_1, π_2 ∈ Irr(G_2(F)), Θ(π_i) has finite length and dim Hom_{H_J}(θ(π_1), θ(π_2)) ≤ dim Hom_{G_2}(π_1, π_2); for τ ∈ Irr(H_J), Θ(τ) has finite length with a unique irreducible quotient (if nonzero). More precisely: (i) PD^× × G_2 gives an injection θ_D : Irr^♥(PD^×) ↪ Irr(G_2(F)), where Irr^♥(PD^×) is the set of representations with nonzero theta lift to G_2; if p ≠ 3 then Irr^♥(PD^×) = Irr(PD^×). (ii) (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 gives an injection θ_B : Irr^♥(PGL_3(F) ⋊ Z/2Z) ↪ Irr(G_2(F)), the subset Irr^♥ can be determined explicitly, and the image of θ_B is disjoint from that of θ_D. (iii) G_2 × PGSp_6 gives an injection θ : Irr(G_2(F)) ∖ Im(θ_D) ↪ Irr(PGSp_6(F)).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.2; proved in §§7, 8, 12 and 15, pp. 2–52 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Assembled from Theorem 7.2 (PD^×), Theorem 8.5 (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) and Theorem 15.1 (PGSp_6). For τ ∈ Irr(PD^×), the nonvanishing of θ_D(τ) is equivalent to τ having nonzero vectors fixed by a maximal torus PE^×; for p ≠ 3 this is Lonka–Tandon (item lonka-tandon). Review note: Status missing is right (route 1). Statement checked against p. 2 in full, including the p ≠ 3 clause of (i) and the disjointness of Im θ_B and Im θ_D in (ii).

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (qualitative properties)
items.statement: The three theta correspondences (i) preserve tempered representations; (ii) any discrete series representation of G_2 lifts to a discrete series representation of precisely one of PD^×, PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp_6; (iii) are functorial for non-tempered representations.
items.note: (i) is Lemma 6.3(i) with Theorems 8.2 and 14.1; (ii) is Corollary 15.7; (iii) is Theorem 15.1(v) and Theorem 8.2. For non-tempered representations 'functorial' means: the L-parameter of the lift is the composite of the L-parameter with the inclusion of dual groups (SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C)).

items.name: Big theta lifts of generic supercuspidal representations of G_2
items.statement: Let π_gen be a Whittaker-generic supercuspidal representation of G_2(F), and Θ(π_gen) its big theta lift to PGSp_6(F). (a) If π_gen is not a theta lift from PGL_3(F) ⋊ Z/2Z, then Θ(π_gen) is an irreducible generic supercuspidal representation of PGSp_6. (b) Otherwise π_gen = θ_B(σ) for a supercuspidal σ ∈ Irr(PGL_3(F) ⋊ Z/2Z). Either σ ≅ Ind_{PGL_3}^{PGL_3⋊Z/2Z}(τ) ≅ Ind_{PGL_3}^{PGL_3⋊Z/2Z}(τ^∨) with τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) supercuspidal and τ ≇ τ^∨, or σ is one of the two extensions τ^+ ≇ τ^− of a supercuspidal τ ≅ τ^∨. (b1) If π_gen = θ_B(Ind(τ)) with τ ≇ τ^∨, then Θ(π_gen) ≅ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ) ≅ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ^∨), where P_3 is the maximal parabolic subgroup of PGSp_6 with Levi factor GL_3. (b2) If π_gen = θ_B(τ^+) with τ ≅ τ^∨, then θ_B(τ^−) = π_deg is an irreducible nongeneric supercuspidal representation of G_2. Moreover Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ) = Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ)_gen ⊕ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ)_deg, with the first summand generic and the second nongeneric, and Θ(π_gen) ≅ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ)_gen, Θ(π_deg) ≅ Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(τ)_deg.
items.locator: §1, p. 3 (arXiv v1); (a) = Corollary 12.5, p. 39; (b) from Theorems 8.5 and 15.2, pp. 27–29 and 52–53
items.note: Completes Savin–Weissman [SWe]. (a) is Corollary 12.5; (b) is Theorems 8.5 and 15.2. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Part (b) is misstated as 'π_gen = θ_B(τ^ε) for a supercuspidal τ of PGL_3'. In case (b1) π_gen is the lift of Ind_{PGL_3}^{PGL_3⋊Z/2Z}(τ) with τ ≇ τ^∨, not of an extension τ^ε. The paper says π_gen is the lift of a supercuspidal representation of PGL_3(F) ⋊ Z/2Z, and then splits the cases by the Clifford description of Irr(PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z). The whole passage is on p. 3; p. 4 begins with the strategy of proof.

items.name: The split octonion algebra
items.statement: O is the split octonion algebra over F: an 8-dimensional non-associative, non-commutative F-algebra with conjugation x ↦ x̄, norm N(x) = x·x̄ = x̄·x and trace Tr(x) = x + x̄. N is a nondegenerate quadratic form. Every x ∈ O satisfies x² − Tr(x)x + N(x) = 0, so for x ∉ F·1 the subalgebra F[x] = F ⊕ Fx is isomorphic to F[t]/(t² − Tr(x)t + N(x)), which is separable iff Tr(x)² ≠ 4N(x). O_0 = ker Tr is the 7-dimensional subspace of trace-zero elements. A nonzero x ∈ O_0 has rank 1 if N(x) = 0 (then x² = 0). Otherwise it has rank 2, and then F[x] ≅ F[t]/(t² + N(x)) is a separable quadratic F-algebra.
items.note: Tau Ceti (f790474) realizes the split octonions over any commutative ring as Zorn vector matrices, with conjugation, trace, the multiplicative norm (norm_mul), the alternative and Moufang laws, and the 7-dimensional imaginary part. The quadratic relation follows from conj_eq_trace_smul_one_sub and self_mul_conj. The rank-1 and rank-2 classification of elements is not stated in the library; it is elementary. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The rank statement is copied from the paper and is false as printed (new issue on §2.1). A nonzero x ∈ O with N(x) ≠ 0 need not generate a separable quadratic algebra. For x = 1, F[x] = F. For x = 1 + n with 0 ≠ n ∈ O_0 and N(n) = 0, N(x) = 1 but F[x] ≅ F[t]/(t−1)². The statement holds for trace-zero x, which is the only case the paper uses. Review note: Library claim checked at f790474 (TauCeti/Algebra/Octonion/Basic.lean): Octonion (l.126), conj (l.327), trace (l.356), norm (l.386), self_mul_conj (l.410), norm_mul (l.427), left_alternative (l.497), imaginary (l.598) and finrank_imaginary (l.628). Cite TauCeti.Octonion.mul_self (l.421: x * x = trace x • x − norm x • 1). It is the public form of the quadratic relation. The note cites Derivation.conj_eq_trace_smul_one_sub, which is private. Not in the library: nondegeneracy of normQuadraticForm (no Nondegenerate or separating lemma in Octonion/), and the rank dichotomy. These two small facts should be marked missing (route 1).

items.name: The exceptional group G_2 = Aut(O)
items.statement: G_2 is the automorphism group of the F-algebra O: a split simple linear algebraic group of rank 2, simply connected and adjoint. Relative to a maximal torus T in a Borel subgroup B, its simple roots are {α, β} with α short and β long, and the highest root is β_0 = 3α + 2β. Following Muić, T ≅ G_m² via t ↦ ((2α + β)(t), (α + β)(t)), so that a pair (χ_1, χ_2) of characters of F^× defines a character χ_1 × χ_2 of T.
items.note: The split group of type G_2 is a Chevalley–Demazure group scheme, planned in Reductive groups, Layer 9. Its Lie algebra as Der(O) is planned in LieHighestWeight, Layer 8 (Mathlib's LieAlgebra.g₂ is the Serre-construction quotient, with no structure theorems; Tau Ceti has derivation lemmas for Octonion). Neither plans the group G_2 = Aut(O) or its identification with the Chevalley group. Review note: Status missing is right for G_2 = Aut(O). mathlib:LieAlgebra.g₂ exists at 082e2d3 (Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/SerreConstruction.lean:164, abbrev g₂ := Matrix.ToLieAlgebra R CartanMatrix.G₂), but it is the Serre Lie algebra, not the group. The split Chevalley group of type G_2 is planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups#layer-9 (pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes over ℤ for every root datum), which route 1 should import. LieHighestWeight Layer 8 plans only Der(O) ≅ g₂. Statement checked: t ↦ ((2α+β)(t), (α+β)(t)) is an isomorphism T ≅ G_m², since {2α+β, α+β} is a ℤ-basis of the root lattice = X^*(T).

items.name: The maximal parabolic subgroups P and Q of G_2
items.statement: Let V_1 ⊂ V_2 ⊂ O_0 be subspaces of dimension 1 and 2 on which octonion multiplication vanishes, P = MN the stabilizer of V_2 and Q = LU that of V_1; P ∩ Q = B is a Borel subgroup. M ≅ GL(V_2) ≅ GL_2 with δ_P = |det|³; N is a 5-dimensional Heisenberg group with centre Z = U_{β_0}, M acts on N/Z by Sym³(F²) ⊗ det^{−1}, and the generic M(F)-orbits on N(F)/Z(F) are parametrized by the isomorphism classes of separable cubic F-algebras. L ≅ GL(V_3/V_1) ≅ GL_2 (V_3 = {x ∈ O_0 : xy = 0 for all y ∈ V_1}) with δ_Q = |det|^5; U is 5-dimensional and 3-step nilpotent, U = U_0 ⊃ U_1 ⊃ U_2 ⊃ U_3 = 1 with U_0/U_1 = U_α × U_{α+β} ≅ F², U_1/U_2 = U_{2α+β} ≅ det and U_2/U_3 = U_{β_0} × U_{β_0−β} ≅ F² ⊗ det as L-modules.
items.note: Review note: Checked by root computation. P's Levi contains α, and N has roots β, α+β, 2α+β, 3α+β (Sym³ ⊗ det^{-1} on N/Z) and centre 3α+2β. Q's Levi contains β. In M ≅ GL_2, det_M = 3α+2β and 2ρ_P = 9α+6β = 3·det_M. In L ≅ GL_2, det_L = 2α+β and 2ρ_Q = 10α+5β = 5·det_L. The L-module structure of U_0/U_1, U_1/U_2 and U_2/U_3 is as stated.

items.name: SL_3 and SU_3 inside G_2
items.statement: The subgroup of G_2 generated by the long root subgroups is isomorphic to SL_3; its normalizer is SL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z, the nontrivial element acting by a pinned outer automorphism. SL_3 is the pointwise stabilizer of a quadratic subalgebra of O isomorphic to F × F, and SL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z its setwise stabilizer. For a subalgebra isomorphic to a quadratic field K/F, the pointwise stabilizer is the quasi-split SU_3^K and the setwise stabilizer SU_3^K ⋊ Z/2Z.

items.name: Subgroups of the dual group G_2(C)
items.statement: The dual group of G_2 is G_2(C), which contains SO_3(C) ⊂ SL_3(C) ⊂ SL_3(C) ⋊ Z/2Z ⊂ G_2(C). The centralizer of SL_3(C) in G_2(C) is μ_3, and that of SO_3(C) is S_3 = μ_3 ⋊ Z/2Z. The centralizer of a long root SL_{2,l}(C) is a short root SL_{2,s}(C) and vice versa, giving SL_{2,l}(C) ×_{μ_2} SL_{2,s}(C) ≅ SO_4(C) ⊂ G_2(C).
items.note: Printed with 'SL_{2,r}(C)' for SL_{2,s}(C) (sourceIssues E1). Also used: G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C), the dual of PGSp_6 (Theorem 15.1(v)). Review note: E1 correction (SL_{2,s}) confirmed on the page image.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (Muić: principal series induced from P)
items.statement: Let M ≅ GL_2 be the Levi factor of P (δ_P = |det|³). For τ ∈ Irr(M) and s ∈ ℝ, let I_P(s, τ) = Ind_P^{G_2}(|det|^s ⊗ τ) (normalized induction) and I_P(τ) = I_P(0, τ). When I_P(s, τ) is a standard module, let J_P(s, τ) be its unique Langlands quotient. I_Q and J_Q are as in Proposition 3.2. π(χ_1, χ_2) is the unitary principal series of GL_2, st is the Steinberg representation of GL_2, and st_χ = st ⊗ (χ∘det). (i) Let τ be unitary supercuspidal. Then I_P(s, τ) is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ (so ω_τ² = 1) and one of the following holds. (a) ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2. Then there is a non-split exact sequence 0 → δ_P(τ) → I_P(1/2, τ) → J_P(1/2, τ) → 0, with δ_P(τ) a generic discrete series representation. (b) ω_τ ≠ 1 and s = 0. Then I_P(0, τ) = I_P(τ)_gen ⊕ I_P(τ)_deg with I_P(τ)_gen generic. (ii) Let τ = st_χ with χ a unitary character of F^×. Then I_P(s, τ) is irreducible except in the following cases. (a) χ = 1 and s = ±3/2 or ±1/2. There is an exact sequence 0 → St_{G_2} → I_P(3/2, st) → J_P(3/2, st) → 0. I_P(1/2, st) has length 3: its unique irreducible submodule π_gen[1] is a generic discrete series representation, its unique irreducible (Langlands) quotient is J_P(1/2, st), and its remaining subquotient is J_Q(1/2, st). (b) χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → π_gen[χ] → I_P(1/2, st_χ) → J_P(1/2, st_χ) → 0, with π_gen[χ] a generic discrete series representation. (c) χ³ = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → π_gen[χ] → I_P(1/2, st_χ) → J_P(1/2, st_χ) → 0, where π_gen[χ] ≅ π_gen[χ^{−1}] is a generic discrete series representation. (iii) Let τ = χ∘det with χ unitary. Then I_P(s, τ) is irreducible except in the following cases. (a) χ = 1 and s = ±3/2 or ±1/2. There is an exact sequence 0 → J_Q(5/2, st) → I_P(3/2, 1) → 1_{G_2} → 0. I_P(1/2, 1) has length 3: its unique irreducible submodule π_deg[1] is a nongeneric discrete series representation, its unique irreducible quotient is J_Q(1, π(1, 1)), and its remaining subquotient is J_Q(1/2, st). (b) χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → J_Q(1/2, st_χ) → I_P(1/2, χ) → J_Q(1, π(1, χ)) → 0. (c) χ³ = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → J_P(1/2, st_{χ^{−1}}) → I_P(1/2, χ) → J_Q(1, π(χ, χ^{−1})) → 0.
items.note: Due almost entirely to Muić ('The unitary dual of p-adic G_2', Duke Math. J. 90 (1997)). The last sequence is stated with the corrected middle term I_P(1/2, χ); the paper prints I_P(1/2, st_χ) (sourceIssues E3). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Two corrections are still needed. (1) Case (i), first bullet: for the 'if and only if' to hold, the reducibility point must be s = ±1/2, not s = 1/2. The contragredient of I_P(s,τ) is I_P(−s, τ^∨), so I_P(−1/2, τ) is also reducible when τ ≅ τ^∨ (new issue). The parameter s is real throughout. (2) Case (iii), second and third bullets: the quotients must be J_Q(1, π(1, χ)) and J_Q(1, π(χ, χ^{−1})), not J_Q(1/2, ·) (new issue). The real exponents of I_Q(1/2, π(χ_1, χ_2)) have half the length of those of I_P(1/2, χ). The same proposition writes J_Q(1, π(1,1)) for χ = 1, and Aubert–Xu (arXiv:2208.12391, (9.3.18), §9.3.38, citing Muić) write J_β(1, π(1, η_2)) and J_β(1, π(η_3^{±1}, η_3^{∓1})). Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound for the E3 correction of the middle term to I_P(1/2, χ), checked on the page image and by an exponent count. The count shows I_P(1/2, st_χ) + I_P(1/2, χ) = Ind_B(χ|·| × χ) with four constituents, and the P-side and Q-side decompositions agree. The item still needs the two further corrections above. Status missing is right: no atlas stage plans Muić's results (route 1).

items.name: Proposition 3.2 (Muić: principal series induced from Q)
items.statement: Let L ≅ GL_2 be the Levi factor of Q (δ_Q = |det|^5). For τ ∈ Irr(L) unitary with L-parameter φ_τ and s ∈ ℝ, let I_Q(s, τ) = Ind_Q^{G_2}(|det|^s ⊗ τ) and I_Q(τ) = I_Q(0, τ). When I_Q(s, τ) is a standard module, let J_Q(s, τ) be its unique Langlands quotient. (i) Let τ be unitary supercuspidal. Then I_Q(s, τ) is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ (so ω_τ² = 1) and one of the following holds. (a) ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → δ_Q(τ) → I_Q(1/2, τ) → J_Q(1/2, τ) → 0, with δ_Q(τ) a generic discrete series representation. (b) ω_τ ≠ 1 (so τ is dihedral), Im(φ_τ) ≅ S_3 and s = ±1. Then 0 → π_gen[τ] → I_Q(1, τ) → J_Q(1, τ) → 0, with π_gen[τ] a generic discrete series representation. (c) ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) ≇ S_3 and s = 0. Then I_Q(0, τ) = I_Q(τ)_gen ⊕ I_Q(τ)_deg with I_Q(τ)_gen generic. (ii) Let τ = st_χ with χ unitary. Then I_Q(s, τ) is irreducible except in the following cases. (a) χ = 1 and s = ±5/2 or ±1/2. Then 0 → St_{G_2} → I_Q(5/2, st) → J_Q(5/2, st) → 0 and 0 → π_gen[1] ⊕ π_deg[1] → I_Q(1/2, st) → J_Q(1/2, st) → 0, with π_gen[1] and π_deg[1] as in Proposition 3.1(ii)(a) and (iii)(a). (b) χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → π_gen[χ] → I_Q(1/2, st_χ) → J_Q(1/2, st_χ) → 0, with π_gen[χ] as in Proposition 3.1(ii)(b). (iii) Let τ = χ∘det with χ unitary. Then I_Q(s, τ) is irreducible except in the following cases. (a) χ = 1 and s = ±5/2 or ±1/2. There is an exact sequence 0 → J_P(3/2, st) → I_Q(5/2, 1) → 1_{G_2} → 0. I_Q(1/2, 1) has length 3: its unique irreducible submodule is J_Q(1/2, st), its unique irreducible quotient is J_Q(1, π(1, 1)), and its remaining subquotient is J_P(1/2, st). (b) χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2. Then 0 → J_P(1/2, st_χ) → I_Q(1/2, χ) → J_Q(1, π(1, χ)) → 0.
items.note: Due to Muić. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Case (iii), second bullet: the quotient must be J_Q(1, π(1, χ)), not J_Q(1/2, π(1, χ)) (new issue). I_Q(1/2, χ) sits in Ind_B with real exponent α+β, a short root, whose dominant conjugate is 2α+β = det_L. So its Langlands quotient is attached to |det_L|^1. This matches J_Q(1, π(1,1)) in case (iii)(a). s is real throughout. Review note: Reducibility points in (i) checked against Shahidi's criterion. For Q the dual unipotent radical carries Sym³ ⊗ det^{-1} ⊕ det, so the pole of L(s, τ, Sym³ ⊗ ω^{-1}) gives s = 1 exactly when Im φ_τ ≅ S_3. For P it carries Std ⊕ det ⊕ Std ⊗ det, giving s = 1/2 for ω_τ = 1 and s = 0 otherwise. The χ = 1 composition series agree with Aubert–Xu (9.3.9)–(9.3.12). Status missing is right (route 1).

items.name: Proposition 3.3 (Borel principal series of G_2)
items.statement: Let β_1, β_2, β_3 be long roots with β_1 + β_2 + β_3 = 0 and, for a character χ of T, χ_i = χ ∘ β_i^∨ (so χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1). Ind_B^{G_2}(χ) is irreducible unless χ_i = |·|^{±1} for some i or χ_i/χ_j = |·|^{±1} for some i ≠ j; or the χ_i are quadratic, nontrivial and pairwise different, in which case Ind_B^{G_2}(χ) = Ind(χ)_gen ⊕ Ind(χ)_deg with the first summand generic.
items.note: Due to Muić. §3.3 also records that a Langlands quotient π of I(s_1, s_2, χ_1, χ_2), s_1 ≥ s_2 ≥ 0, embeds in I(−s_1, −s_2, χ_1^{−1}, χ_2^{−1}) = I_P(π(χ_1^{−1}|·|^{−s_1}, χ_2^{−1}|·|^{−s_2})), and in I_P(−s + 1/2, χ_1^{−1}) when χ_1 = χ_2 and s_1 = s_2 + 1 ≥ 1. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): The statement is correct. The note copies the paper's undefined variable (new issue on §3.3). It should read: π ↪ I_P(−s_1 + 1/2, χ_1^{−1}) when χ_1 = χ_2 and s_1 = s_2 + 1 ≥ 1. Here I_P(−s_1 + 1/2, χ_1^{−1}) is induced from the one-dimensional submodule χ_1^{−1}|·|^{−s_1+1/2}∘det of π(χ_1^{−1}|·|^{−s_1}, χ_1^{−1}|·|^{−s_1+1}). Review note: Checked. The coroots β_i^∨ of three long roots summing to 0 are short coroots and generate X_*(T), since G_2 is simply connected. The long coroots are ±(β_i^∨ − β_j^∨), so Rodier's condition χ∘a^∨ = |·|^{±1} becomes χ_i = |·|^{±1} or χ_i/χ_j = |·|^{±1}. The (χ_1, χ_2, χ_3) bookkeeping is reused in §8.3 (p. 25).

items.name: Non-tempered irreducible representations of G_2
items.statement: Every irreducible non-tempered representation of G_2 is the unique irreducible quotient of exactly one of: (a) I_Q(τ) with τ an unramified twist of a tempered representation of L ≅ GL_2 with |ω_τ| = |·|^s, s > 0; (b) I_P(τ) with τ such a twist on M ≅ GL_2; (c) I_P(τ) with τ the unique quotient of a representation of GL_2 induced from characters χ_1, χ_2 with |χ_i| = |·|^{s_i}, s_1 > s_2 > 0. The quotients are written J_Q(τ) in case (a) and J_P(τ) in cases (b) and (c).
items.note: The Langlands classification for G_2, with Muić's results. Its analogue for PGSp_6 is item nontempered-pgsp6. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. Exhaustion ('these exhaust the irreducible nontempered representations') and the uniqueness implicit in 'exactly one' come from the Langlands classification (with Muić), which the paper uses without proof. The Langlands classification is not planned in SR (see item smooth-rep-tools).

items.name: L-parameters and conjectural L-packets of G_2
items.statement: An L-parameter of G_2 is an admissible homomorphism ϕ : WD_F = W_F × SL_2(C) → G_2(C), up to G_2(C)-conjugacy, with component group A_ϕ = π_0(Z_{G_2(C)}(ϕ)). The LLC desiderata ask for L-packets Π_ϕ = {π(ρ) : ρ ∈ Â_ϕ} that partition Irr(G_2). Non-tempered: every non-tempered irreducible representation is uniquely a Langlands quotient J_P(τ), J_Q(τ) or J_B(χ). Its parameter is the LLC parameter of the Levi datum (GL_2 or GL_1 × GL_1) composed with the inclusion of the dual Levi into G_2(C). These packets are singletons with A_ϕ = 1, and the non-tempered representations correspond to the parameters with ϕ(W_F) unbounded. Tempered but not square-integrable: each such representation is uniquely a summand of a representation induced from a unitary discrete series of a proper Levi factor, and gets the composite parameter. Then ϕ(W_F) is bounded and ϕ(WD_F) lies in a proper Levi subgroup. |Π_ϕ| ∈ {1, 2} equals |A_ϕ|, and each packet has a unique generic member, assigned to the trivial character. Discrete series parameters (ϕ not factoring through a proper Levi subgroup; equivalently Z_{G_2(C)}(ϕ) finite) are sorted by ϕ(SL_2), and all their non-supercuspidal members are listed. (1) ϕ(SL_2) is the principal SL_2: A_ϕ = 1 and Π_ϕ = {St_{G_2}}. (2) ϕ(SL_2) = SO_3 ⊂ SL_3 ⊂ G_2(C), the subregular SL_2, whose centralizer is S_3; so ϕ|W_F is φ : W_F → S_3. (a) φ(W_F) = 1: A_ϕ = S_3 and Π_ϕ = {π(1) = π_gen[1], π(r) = π_deg[1], π(ε) = π_sc[1]}, where 1, r, ε are the trivial, 2-dimensional and sign representations of S_3. π_sc[1] is the depth-zero supercuspidal representation induced from the inflation to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of the cuspidal unipotent representation G_2[1] of G_2(F_q). (b) φ(W_F) = μ_2, which gives a quadratic character χ by class field theory: A_ϕ = μ_2 and Π_ϕ = {π(1) = π_gen[χ], π(−1)}. If χ is unramified, π(−1) = π_sc[−1] is the depth-zero supercuspidal representation obtained from G_2[−1]. (c) φ(W_F) = μ_3, which gives a cubic character χ: A_ϕ = μ_3 and Π_ϕ = {π(1) = π_gen[χ], π(ω), π(ω²)}. If χ is unramified, π(ω) = π_sc[ω] and π(ω²) = π_sc[ω²] are obtained from G_2[ω] and G_2[ω²]. (d) φ(W_F) = S_3: r∘φ is the parameter of a supercuspidal representation τ of GL_2, A_ϕ = 1 and Π_ϕ = {π_gen[τ]} (Proposition 3.2(i)). (3) ϕ(SL_2) = SL_{2,s}, a short root SL_2, with centralizer SL_{2,l}. Then ϕ|W_F is φ : W_F → SL_{2,l}, the parameter of a supercuspidal τ of GL_2 with trivial central character (so τ ≅ τ^∨). A_ϕ = μ_2 and Π_ϕ = {π(1) = δ_P(τ), π(−1)} with π(−1) supercuspidal. (4) ϕ(SL_2) = SL_{2,l}, a long root SL_2, with centralizer SL_{2,s}, a short root SL_2. Then ϕ|W_F is φ : W_F → SL_{2,s}, the parameter of a supercuspidal τ of GL_2 with trivial central character. A_ϕ = μ_2 and Π_ϕ = {π(1) = δ_Q(τ), π(−1)} with π(−1) supercuspidal. (5) ϕ(SL_2) = 1: Π_ϕ consists of supercuspidal representations. Every non-supercuspidal discrete series representation of G_2 appears in this list.
items.note: A partial local Langlands correspondence (desiderata), not a theorem at this point; the queued PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B proves the correspondence using this paper. In item (4) the paper calls SL_{2,s} 'a long root SL_2' (sourceIssues E2). The noncuspidal discrete series are all accounted for. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Two omissions make the item ambiguous. In (2) with φ(W_F) = S_3, the item does not say which τ appears in Π_ϕ = {π_gen[τ]}: it is the supercuspidal τ of GL_2 with parameter r∘φ. In (4), it omits that ϕ|W_F is φ : W_F → SL_{2,s} with τ of trivial central character, that A_ϕ = μ_2, and that π(−1) is supercuspidal. The E2 correction is right. The assignments in (3) and (4) are consistent with Propositions 3.1(i) and 3.2(i): M^∨ is a long-root GL_2 and L^∨ a short-root GL_2 in G_2(C).

items.name: Local Fourier coefficients along N indexed by cubic algebras
items.statement: The M-orbits of 1-dimensional characters of N (the unipotent radical of P) are indexed by cubic F-algebras, the generic orbits by étale cubic algebras E; ψ_E denotes a character in the orbit of E, and π_{N,ψ_E} the twisted Jacquet module of a representation π of G_2.
items.note: Review note: Status missing is right. SR.2 plans N-coinvariants and Jacquet functors but does not name twisted coinvariants π_{N,ψ} or their exactness (Bernstein–Zelevinsky). Route 3 (SR.2/SR.3) should state the twisted version, which Lemma 3.4 and §6 rely on.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 (nonvanishing and finiteness of degenerate coefficients)
items.statement: For every irreducible, nongeneric, infinite-dimensional representation π of G_2 there is an étale cubic F-algebra E with π_{N,ψ_E} ≠ 0; moreover π_{N,ψ_E} is finite-dimensional for every étale E.
items.note: Proof by citation: the wave-front set of such π is supported on subregular nilpotent orbits, parametrized by cubic étale algebras (Huang–Magaard–Savin; Loke–Savin); nonvanishing and finite-dimensionality are Mœglin–Waldspurger's theory of degenerate Whittaker models (Math. Z. 196 (1987)) and Varma's extension to residual characteristic 2 (Math. Z. 277 (2014)). These are general p-adic results that no layer of the atlas plans. Review note: Status missing is right. The two inputs of the proof are proposed as separate items (see coverage): the Mœglin–Waldspurger/Varma theorem (route 3) and the wave-front statement for G_2 (route 1). Lemma 3.4 is used in the dichotomy proof (§6.5, p. 21) and for Proposition 6.6.

items.name: Freudenthal–Jordan algebras and the Lie algebras g_J
items.statement: Let J be a Freudenthal–Jordan F-algebra with cubic norm form N_J and M_J = {g ∈ GL(J) : N_J ∘ g = N_J}. The space g_J = sl_3 ⊕ Lie(M_J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ J)^* carries the structure of a simple exceptional Lie algebra, of type G_2, D_4, E_6, E_7 for dim J = 1, 3, 9, 15. If dim J = 3, J is a cubic étale algebra E. If dim J = 9, J is the space of ι-symmetric elements of a central simple algebra B_K over an étale quadratic K with an involution ι of the second kind; the split case is J = M_3(F), with Aut(M_3) = PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z. If dim J = 15, J = H_3(B_F), the 3 × 3 Hermitian matrices over a quaternion algebra B_F, split when B_F = M_2(F). G_J is the identity component of Aut(g_J); for dim J = 9 there is a (not necessarily split) extension 1 → G_J → Aut(g_J) → Z/2Z → 1.
items.note: Following Gan–Savin, 'On minimal representations: definitions and properties' (Represent. Theory 9 (2005)) and Knus–Merkurjev–Rost–Tignol. LieHighestWeight Layer 8 plans explicit split E_6 and E_7 over a characteristic-0 field and names the magic square as one route, but not these forms over a p-adic field, the non-split E_6^D, or Aut(J). Tau Ceti's AlbertAlgebra is the 27-dimensional H_3(O), not used here. The paper writes the pair as (B_K, τ) and then the involution as ι (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: The dual pairs G_2 × Aut(J)
items.statement: The centralizer of Aut(J) in g_J is sl_3 ⊕ (F³ ⊗ 1_J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ 1_J)^* ≅ g_F, a Lie algebra of type G_2. This gives a dual pair G_2 × Aut(J) ⊂ Aut(G_J). For dim J = 9 there is an exact sequence of algebraic groups 1 → Aut(J)⁰ → Aut(J) → Z/2Z → 1, where Aut(J)⁰ = PGU(B_K, ι) is adjoint of type A_2. The cases used, with H_J = Aut(J)(F), are as follows. For J = D^+ with D a cubic division algebra, G_J = E_6^D and H_J = PD^× (Aut(D^+)(F) = PD^×, since D ≇ D^op). For J = M_3(F)^+, the dual pair lies in Aut(g_J) = E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and H_J = PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z. For J = H_3(M_2(F)), G_J = E_7 and H_J = PGSp_6. The groups of type E are adjoint.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: (1) The centralizer is stated correctly with (F³ ⊗ 1_J)^*, but the paper prints F³ ⊗ 1_J twice (new issue on §4.2). (2) The item gives both the surjection Aut(J) → Z/2Z and H_J = Aut(J) = PD^× for J = D^+. The sequence is exact as algebraic groups, but for J = D^+ the non-identity component has no F-points: a Jordan automorphism of D^+ that is an anti-automorphism would be an isomorphism D ≅ D^op, impossible for a cubic division algebra. So H_J is the group of F-points, as in the table of §4.4. (3) The locator should include the table of §4.4, p. 16.

items.name: The dual pairs Aut(i : E → J) × G_E
items.statement: For an embedding i : E → J of a cubic étale algebra, H_{J,E} = Aut(i : E → J) ⊂ Aut(J) (for dim J = 9 its identity component is a 2-dimensional torus; see [GS14]). The centralizer of H_{J,E} in g_J contains g_E = sl_3 ⊕ t_E ⊕ F³ ⊗ E ⊕ (F³ ⊗ E)^*, t_E ≅ E^0 the trace-zero elements, which is Lie(G_E) for G_E = Spin_8^E, the simply connected quasi-split group attached to E; this gives a (non-injective) map H_{J,E} × G_E → Aut(G_J). H_{J,E} is PE^×, PE^× ⋊ Z/2Z and SL_2(E)/μ_2 for J = D^+, M_3(F)^+ and H_3(M_2(F)); for J = D^+, E is necessarily a field.

items.name: The see-saw (4.1) and the see-saw identity (5.1)
items.statement: The dual pairs G_2 × H_J and H_{J,E} × G_E form a see-saw in Aut(G_J): G_2 ⊂ G_E = Spin_8^E and H_{J,E} ⊂ H_J. For π ∈ Irr(G_2): Hom_{H_{J,E}}(Θ(π), C) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(R_J(E), π) (5.1), where R_J(E) = Θ(1) is the big theta lift of the trivial representation of H_{J,E} to Spin_8^E.
items.note: The diagram (4.1) prints G_E := Spin_4^E for Spin_8^E (sourceIssues E5). Review note: E5 confirmed on the page image; identity (5.1) checked by computing Hom_{H_{J,E}×G_2}(Π_J, 1 ⊗ π) in two ways.

items.name: Minimal representations and big theta lifts for exceptional dual pairs
items.statement: Π_J is the minimal representation of the adjoint group G_J (Gan–Savin 2005), extended to E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z so that Z/2Z fixes the spherical vector. For a dual pair G × H in G_J and π ∈ Irr(G), the maximal π-isotypic quotient of Π_J, Π/∩_{φ ∈ Hom_G(Π, π)} ker φ, is π ⊗ Θ(π) for a smooth representation Θ(π) of H (MVW, Lemme III.4); Θ(π) is the big theta lift and its cosocle (maximal semisimple quotient) θ(π). π has nonzero theta lift if Θ(π) ≠ 0, equivalently Hom_G(Π, π) ≠ 0; lifts from H to G are defined in the same way. Π_J is defined over R, so Θ(π̄) is the complex conjugate of Θ(π).
items.note: The minimal representations of E_6, E_6^D, E_7, Spin_8^E and SO_2n are inputs from Gan–Savin 2005, Magaard–Savin and Loke–Savin; nothing in the atlas plans minimal representations. MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 plans big theta modules only for the Weil representation of classical dual pairs.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (R_J(E) and the degenerate principal series of Spin_8^E)
items.statement: Let P_E = M_E N_E ⊂ Spin_8^E be the Heisenberg parabolic, M_E ≅ GL_2(E)⁰, and I_E(s) = Ind_{P_E}^{Spin_8^E} |det|^s. Then R_J(E) ↪ I_E(s_J) with s_J = −1/2 for J = D^+ or M_3(F)^+ and s_J = 1/2 for J = H_3(M_2(F)). I_E(1/2) has length 3 if E is a field and length 2 otherwise, with a unique irreducible submodule V and quotient R_{M_3(F)}(E) ⊕ R_D(E) (R_D(E) = 0 if E is not a field); there are exact sequences 0 → R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E) → I_E(1/2) → R_D(E) → 0 and 0 → V → R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E) → R_{M_3(F)}(E) → 0. In particular I_E(1/2) = R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E) if E is not a field.
items.note: Cited from Gan–Savin, 'A family of Arthur packets of triality Spin(8)', a 2015 preprint, and Segal (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 372 (2019)), for the module structure of I_E(s). A paper of Gan and Savin on Arthur packets for triality Spin_8 appeared in 2022 (Pure Appl. Math. Q. 18; arXiv:2106.06460); whether it contains the embedding R_J(E) ↪ I_E(s_J) as used was not checked.

items.name: Proposition 5.3 (vanishing of Ext¹)
items.statement: Assume E is a field. If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is tempered or has cuspidal support different from that of π_deg[1], then Ext¹_{G_2}(R_D(E), π) = 0, so 0 → Hom_{G_2}(R_D(E), π) → Hom_{G_2}(I_E(1/2), π) → Hom_{G_2}(R_{H_3(M_2(F))}(E), π) → 0 is exact.
items.note: As a G_2-module, R_D(E) is the direct sum of a supercuspidal representation (of infinite length) and π_deg[1], a constituent of I_Q(1/2, st) (Savin [Sa]); discrete series are projective in the category of tempered representations. Review note: missing is right. The Ext^1 input it needs, Ext^1_{G_2}(π_deg[1], π) = 0 for tempered π in the category of all smooth representations (not only in the tempered category), is Meyer's/Opdam–Solleveld's theorem; it belongs to item cuspidal-semisimple (route 3, SR.3), whose statement should be sharpened to that form (see coverage).

items.name: Proposition 5.4 (I_E(s) restricted to G_2)
items.statement: As a G_2-representation, I_E(s) has an equivariant filtration 0 ⊂ I_0 ⊂ I_1 ⊂ I_2 ⊂ I_3 ⊂ I_4 with I_0 ≅ ind_N^{G_2} ψ̄_E, I_1/I_0 ≅ I_P(s/2 + 1/4, C_c^∞(PGL_2)), I_2/I_1 ≅ m_E · I_P(s/2 + 1/4, ind_N^{PGL_2} ψ), I_3/I_2 ≅ m_E · I_Q(s + 1) and I_4/I_3 ≅ I_P(s + 1), where m_E = 3, 1, 0 for E = F³, F × K, a field. Hence 0 → ind_N^{G_2} ψ̄_E → I_E(s) → Σ_E(s) → 0 and an exact sequence 0 → Hom(Σ_E(s), π) → Hom(I_E(s), π) → Hom_N(π^∨, ψ_E) → Ext¹_{G_2}(Σ_E(s), π).
items.note: Mackey theory for the G_2-orbits on Spin_8^E/P_E. The paper calls it 'a key technical result' and gives no proof in arXiv v1 beyond the statement. Review note: missing is right; no stage plans restrictions of degenerate principal series of Spin_8^E. The proof is absent in arXiv v1 (E20, confirmed).

items.name: Proposition 5.5 and Lemma 5.6
items.statement: If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is tempered or has cuspidal support along Q, then Hom_{G_2}(I_E(1/2), π) ≅ Hom_N(π^∨, ψ_E). Lemma 5.6: for such π, Ext^i_{G_2}(J_j, π) = 0 for all i and all successive quotients J_j = I_j/I_{j−1} (j = 1, …, 4) of Proposition 5.4 at s = 1/2.
items.note: Proof of Lemma 5.6: second adjointness reduces to central characters; for tempered π the centre of M acts on r_P(π) by characters of absolute value |z|^t with t ≤ 0, while it acts on |det|^{1/2} C_c^∞(PGL_2) by |z|. The paper treats J_1 and says 'the other cases are dealt with in the same way'.

items.name: Lemma 6.2 (finiteness of the noncuspidal part)
items.statement: For each of the three J: (i) for π ∈ Irr(G_2), write Θ_J(π) = Θ_J(π)_c ⊕ Θ_J(π)_nc (cuspidal and noncuspidal components); then Θ_J(π)_nc has finite length, so Θ_J(π) has an irreducible quotient if nonzero. (ii) The same holds for τ ∈ Irr(H_J) and Θ_J(τ).
items.note: J = D^+ from Savin [Sa], J = M_3(F)^+ from [GS04], J = H_3(M_2(F)) from §§13–14. For H_J = PGSp_6 the tempered case is §14.2, and §14.3 treats Θ(σ)_nc only for the top pieces of the filtrations, 'leaving the details to the reader' (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (temperedness is preserved; non-tempered representations lift to PGSp_6)
items.statement: (i) If π ∈ Irr(G_2) and τ ∈ Irr(H_J) with π ⊗ τ a quotient of Π_J, then π is tempered if and only if τ is tempered. (ii) Every non-tempered π ∈ Irr(G_2) has nonzero theta lift to PGSp_6.
items.note: From Savin [Sa] (PD^×), [GS04] (PGL_3) and Theorem 14.1 (PGSp_6).

items.name: Lemma 6.4 (a chain of containments of periods)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered, J ∈ {D^+, M_3(F)^+, H_3(M_2(F))}, E an étale cubic F-algebra with an embedding i : E → J (so E is a cubic field when J = D^+), H_{J,E} = Aut(i : E → J), and τ ∈ Irr(H_J) tempered with Hom_{G_2 × H_J}(Π_J, π ⊠ τ) ≠ 0. Then Hom_N(π, ψ_E) ⊆ Hom_N(Θ(τ), ψ_E) ≅ Hom_{H_{J,E}}(τ^∨, C) ⊆ Hom_{H_{J,E}}(Θ(π^∨), C) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(R_J(E), π^∨), and if one of these spaces is finite-dimensional, all the inclusions are isomorphisms.
items.note: Uses (Π_J)_{N,ψ_E} ≅ ind_{H_{J,E}}^{H_J}(1) (item minimal-rep-coefficients), the see-saw identity, and Propositions 5.3 and 5.5, which give dim Hom(R_J(E), π^∨) ≤ dim Hom(I_E(1/2), π^∨) = dim Hom_N(π, ψ_E) (6.5). The first instance of the paper's 'ping-pong with periods'. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The étale cubic algebra E is not quantified. The chain uses the see-saw for an embedding i : E → J, so E must embed in J: for J = D^+ it must be a cubic field (H_{J,E} is undefined otherwise). The paper leaves this implicit too (new issue on Lemma 6.4/§6.5).

items.name: Proposition 6.6
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(H_J) be tempered and π ∈ Irr(G_2) a tempered, non-generic quotient of Θ_J(τ). Then π is the unique irreducible tempered quotient of Θ_J(τ).

items.name: Proposition 6.7
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and non-generic. Then Θ_J(π) cannot have two tempered irreducible quotients; in particular its cuspidal component Θ_J(π)_c is irreducible or 0.
items.note: Θ_J(π)_c is semisimple because the groups have compact centre (item cuspidal-semisimple).

items.name: Corollary 6.8
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and non-generic. Then Θ_J(π) has finite length; if Θ_J(π) ≠ 0 it has a unique irreducible quotient θ(π), which is tempered; and for tempered non-generic π_1, π_2, θ(π_1) ≅ θ(π_2) implies π_1 ≅ π_2.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 (Savin: the dual pair PD^× × G_2)
items.statement: Let Π_D = ⊕_{τ ∈ Irr(PD^×)} τ ⊠ Θ(τ) be the minimal representation of E_6^D restricted to PD^× × G_2. (i) Θ(1) = π_deg[1]. (ii) For τ nontrivial, Θ(τ) is a nongeneric supercuspidal representation of finite length (possibly 0). (iii) For χ = χ_0 ∘ Nrd with χ_0 a nontrivial unramified cubic character of F^×, Θ(χ) and Θ(χ²) are the two depth-zero supercuspidal representations π_sc[ω], π_sc[ω²] of §3.4 (2), third bullet (the paper writes π_sc[χ], π_sc[χ²] and does not say which is which). (iv) For each cubic field E/F, Hom_N(Θ(τ), ψ_E) ≅ Hom_{PE^×}(τ, C).
items.note: Savin, 'A class of supercuspidal representations of G_2(k)', Canad. Math. Bull. 42 (1999). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Part (iii) names the lifts π_sc[χ], π_sc[χ²], but §3.4 (2), third bullet (p. 13), to which it refers, names the two depth-zero supercuspidals π_sc[ω] and π_sc[ω²] (= π(ω), π(ω²)). The labels π_sc[χ] are never defined (new misprint). Parts (i), (ii) and (iv) are exact.

items.name: Theorem 7.2 (Howe duality for PD^× × G_2)
items.statement: (i) For τ ∈ Irr(PD^×), Θ(τ) is irreducible if nonzero. (ii) If Θ(τ_1) ≅ Θ(τ_2) ≠ 0 then τ_1 ≅ τ_2. (iii) If p ≠ 3, τ ↦ Θ(τ) is an injection Irr(PD^×) ↪ Irr(G_2). Hence dim Hom_{G_2}(θ(τ_1), θ(τ_2)) ≤ dim Hom_{PD^×}(τ_1, τ_2), and Θ(π) is irreducible or zero for every π ∈ Irr(G_2).
items.note: (i)–(ii) from Propositions 6.6 and 6.7; (iii) from Proposition 7.1(iv) and Lonka–Tandon. The paper labels the parts (i), (ii), (ii) (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Torus-fixed vectors in representations of PD^× (Lonka–Tandon)
items.statement: If p ≠ 3, every irreducible representation τ of PD^× (D a cubic division algebra) has a nonzero vector fixed by PE^× for some cubic field E ⊂ D (Lonka–Tandon, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 33 (2018), Th. 2.4).
items.locator: §1 and proof of Theorem 7.2, pp. 2–23 (arXiv v1)
items.note: For p = 3 the question is open, which is why θ_D is only known to be injective on Irr^♥(PD^×).

items.name: Representations of PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z
items.statement: Z/2Z acts on GL_3 by the pinned automorphism A ↦ w_0 ᵗA^{−1} w_0^{−1}, w_0 = antidiag(1, −1, 1). For a Z/2Z-invariant Whittaker character ψ of the upper unipotent U, ψ ⊗ 1 and ψ ⊗ sign are its two extensions to U ⋊ Z/2Z. For τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3): if τ^∨ ≇ τ, then τ^+ := Ind_{PGL_3}^H τ ≅ Ind τ^∨ is irreducible, and for generic τ both Hom_{U⋊Z/2Z}(τ^+, ψ ⊗ 1) and Hom_{U⋊Z/2Z}(τ^+, ψ ⊗ sign) are one-dimensional. If τ ≅ τ^∨, it has two extensions to H = PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z, which differ by the unique nontrivial character sign of H; for generic τ, τ^+ is the extension with Hom_{U⋊Z/2Z}(τ^+, ψ ⊗ 1) one-dimensional and τ^− is the other. The nongeneric self-dual irreducible representations of PGL_3 are the trivial representation and the Langlands quotients J_B(μ), μ = χ|·|^{1/2} ⊗ 1 ⊗ χ|·|^{−1/2} with χ² = 1. For these, the cosocle θ(τ) of the theta lift of τ from PGL_3 to G_2 is irreducible (the paper cites [GS04] for J_B(μ) only). τ^+ is defined by θ(τ^+) = θ(τ) and θ(τ^−) = 0. Every irreducible representation of H is self-dual.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The item repeats the paper's claim that 'the only nongeneric and self-dual representations of PGL_3 are the Langlands quotients J_B(μ), μ = χ|·|^{1/2} ⊗ 1 ⊗ χ|·|^{−1/2}, χ² = 1'. That claim is false: the trivial representation of PGL_3 = J_B(|·| ⊗ 1 ⊗ |·|^{−1}) is nongeneric, self-dual and not of that form. So τ^± is left undefined for τ = 1, which Theorems 8.2(ii) and 8.5(i) cover, since φ_1 = |·| ⊕ 1 ⊕ |·|^{−1} contains the trivial representation (new issue). The item also omits the element w_0.

items.name: Lemma 8.1 (Whittaker and Fourier coefficients of the E_6 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let Π be the minimal representation of split E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z. (i) For a Whittaker character ψ_V of G_2, Π_{V,ψ_V} ≅ ind_{U ⋊ Z/2Z}^H(ψ ⊗ 1), so Hom_V(Θ(τ^ε), ψ_V) ≅ Hom_{U⋊Z/2Z}(τ^ε, ψ ⊗ 1). (ii) For an étale cubic algebra E, Hom_N(Θ(τ^ε), ψ_E) ≅ Hom_{PE^× ⋊ Z/2Z}(τ^ε, C).
items.note: 'Basic computations', not proved in the paper. Review note: missing is right. Part (ii) without the Z/2Z refinement is the case J = M_3(F) of Gross–Savin's Lemma 2.9, already cited in Lemma 6.4 (item minimal-rep-coefficients). The Z/2Z refinement in (i) and (ii) is unproved (E21, confirmed).

items.name: Theorem 8.2 (the results of [GS04] for PGL_3 × G_2)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) with L-parameter φ_τ : WD_F → SL_3(C): if τ is non-supercuspidal, Θ(τ) has finite length; if τ ≇ τ^∨ is supercuspidal, Θ(τ) is irreducible supercuspidal (this covers all τ if p ≠ 2); θ(τ^ε) denotes the maximal semisimple quotient of Θ(τ^ε). (i) If τ ≇ τ^∨, θ(τ^+) is irreducible and nonzero; if τ is supercuspidal, discrete series or tempered, so is θ(τ^+); if τ is generic and tempered (more generally, if the G_2 standard module with parameter φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C) is irreducible), θ(τ^+) is generic, and this fails otherwise (printed for all generic τ); if τ is not supercuspidal, θ(τ^+) is not supercuspidal and its L-parameter is φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C). (ii) If τ ≅ τ^∨ and φ_τ contains the trivial representation (this includes τ = 1_{PGL_3}), θ(τ^−) = 0 and θ(τ^+) is nonzero, irreducible, not discrete series, with parameter φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C). (iii) If τ ≅ τ^∨ and φ_τ does not contain the trivial representation: for τ = St, θ(St^+) ⊕ θ(St^−) = π_gen[1] ⊕ π_sc[1]; for τ tempered, induced from a supercuspidal σ ≅ σ^∨ of GL_2 with nontrivial central character, θ(τ^+) ⊕ θ(τ^−) = Ind_P^{G_2}(σ)_gen ⊕ Ind_P^{G_2}(σ)_deg; for τ the tempered principal series from nontrivial quadratic χ_1, χ_2, χ_3 with χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1, θ(τ^+) ⊕ θ(τ^−) = Ind_B^{G_2}(χ)_gen ⊕ Ind_B^{G_2}(χ)_deg; for τ self-dual supercuspidal (p = 2), Θ(τ^ε) is supercuspidal and Θ(τ^+) ⊕ Θ(τ^−) = π_gen ⊕ π_deg, with π_gen generic irreducible supercuspidal and π_deg nongeneric supercuspidal of unknown length.
items.note: Gan–Savin, 'Endoscopic lifts from PGL_3 to G_2', Compos. Math. 140 (2004), combined with §8.1. Self-dual supercuspidals of PGL_3 need p = 2: an irreducible 3-dimensional orthogonal parameter has primitive image A_4 or S_4, which needs wild ramification at 2. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Part (i) says 'if τ is generic … so is θ(τ^+)' and, for τ not supercuspidal, that θ(τ^+) has L-parameter φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C). These two claims are incompatible for nontempered generic τ whose composite G_2 parameter has a reducible standard module. For example, take τ = Ind_B^{PGL_3}(|·| ⊗ μ ⊗ |·|^{−1}μ^{−1}) with μ unitary and μ² ≠ 1. This τ is irreducible, generic and not self-dual. Ind_B^{G_2}(χ) with χ_1 = |·| is reducible (§3.3), so the Langlands quotient with that parameter is nongeneric. By [GS04] (functoriality for non-supercuspidal τ) the genericity clause is the one that fails (new issue). In (ii) the item drops 'nonzero' from 'θ(τ^+) is nonzero irreducible'.

items.name: Lemma 8.3 (a twisted Jacquet module of the E_6 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let ψ be a nontrivial character of [U, U], trivial on the centre Z_U of U (U the unipotent radical of Q). Then Π_{[U,U],ψ} ≅ ind_{GL_2 ⋊ Z/2Z}^{PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z}(C_c(M_2(F))) as (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × SL_2-modules, SL_2 = [L, L], where C_c(M_2(F)) is the Weil representation of O_3 × SL_2 for the determinant form (GL_2 acting by conjugation, Z/2Z by X ↦ w ᵗX w^{−1}) and GL_2 ↪ PGL_3 by (a b; c d) ↦ (a 0 b; 0 1 0; c 0 d).
items.note: The paper says it 'follows by a standard computation' and gives none. Review note: missing is right; no proof or reference in arXiv v1 (E21, confirmed). Needed only for self-dual supercuspidal τ, so only when p = 2.

items.name: Proposition 8.4 (a miracle of Oberwolfach)
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) be self-dual supercuspidal. Then Θ(τ^−) ≠ 0.
items.note: Proof: τ^− is a quotient of the SL_2-coinvariants of Π_{[U,U],ψ}, via Lemma 8.3, the even/odd Weil representations of S̃L_2 and their theta lifts to O_3 (item sl2-o3-theta), and the fact that every generic representation of GL_2, in particular st, is a quotient of τ|_{GL_2} (item prasad-restriction). Review note: missing is right. The hypothesis is non-vacuous only for p = 2: a self-dual supercuspidal of PGL_3 has a primitive 3-dimensional orthogonal parameter.

items.name: Theorem 8.5 (Howe duality for (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3) with L-parameter φ_τ, and τ^ε as in §8.1 (with the trivial representation added to the nongeneric self-dual case): (i) Θ(τ^ε) = 0 if and only if φ_τ contains the trivial representation (so τ ≅ τ^∨) and ε = −. (ii) For ε = ±, Θ(τ^ε) has finite length and, if nonzero, a unique irreducible quotient θ(τ^ε). (iii) If θ(τ^ε) is generic, then τ is generic and ε = +. Conversely, if τ is generic, ε = +, and τ is tempered (more generally, the G_2 standard module with parameter φ_τ composed with SL_3(C) ⊂ G_2(C) is irreducible), then θ(τ^+) is generic. (iv) If θ(τ^ε) ≠ 0 and τ is discrete series (resp. tempered), so is θ(τ^ε); θ(τ^ε) is supercuspidal iff τ is supercuspidal or τ^ε = St^−. (v) θ(τ_1^{ε_1}) ≅ θ(τ_2^{ε_2}) ≠ 0 implies τ_1^{ε_1} ≅ τ_2^{ε_2}. Hence dim Hom_{G_2}(θ(τ_1^{ε_1}), θ(τ_2^{ε_2})) ≤ dim Hom_{PGL_3⋊Z/2Z}(τ_1^{ε_1}, τ_2^{ε_2}), and for π ∈ Irr(G_2), Θ(π) is a representation of PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z of finite length with a unique irreducible quotient if nonzero.
items.note: The proof uses Lemma 8.1 (to put π_gen[1] into θ(St^+)), Proposition 6.6, Proposition 8.4, the Jacquet module of the E_7 minimal representation along P_3 (Magaard–Savin) and Savin–Weissman's result that a generic representation cannot lift to two different generic representations of PGSp_6. Two slips in the proof: E7 and E8. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: (1) Part (iii) is taken from the paper, but its 'if' direction (τ generic and ε = + ⇒ θ(τ^+) generic) fails for nontempered generic τ whose composite G_2 standard module is reducible, e.g. τ = Ind_B^{PGL_3}(|·| ⊗ μ ⊗ |·|^{−1}μ^{−1}) with μ unitary, μ² ≠ 1. It is 'summarized from Theorem 8.2', whose part (i) contradicts itself there (new issue). (2) The labels τ^± are undefined for the trivial representation of PGL_3, which part (i) covers (new issue on §8.1). (3) The paper's last sentence says Θ(π) is a finite-length representation 'of PGL_3'; it must be 'of PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z', since as a PGL_3-representation θ(π) = τ ⊕ τ^∨ when τ ≇ τ^∨. The item already drops 'of PGL_3'.

items.name: Generic quotients of restrictions from GL_3 to GL_2
items.statement: Let τ be an irreducible generic representation of GL_3(F) (in particular of PGL_3(F)), and embed GL_2 ↪ GL_3 by (a b; c d) ↦ (a 0 b; 0 1 0; c 0 d). Then every irreducible generic representation σ of GL_2(F), in particular the Steinberg representation st, is a quotient of τ|_{GL_2}: Hom_{GL_2}(τ, σ) ≠ 0. In fact it is one-dimensional (D. Prasad, Duke Math. J. 69 (1993)).
items.note: Stated as 'it is known' without a reference. It is D. Prasad's theorem on GL_3 restricted to GL_2 (Duke Math. J. 69 (1993)), a case of the Gan–Gross–Prasad branching for GL. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The quantifiers are loose: 'a quotient of the restriction … of an irreducible generic representation τ' reads as an existence statement. The paper applies it to the given self-dual supercuspidal τ, so it needs the statement for every generic τ. Review note: missing is defensible, but the part used (non-vanishing) follows from the GL_3 × GL_2 local Rankin–Selberg integrals that AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3 plans. The integral normalized by L(s, τ × σ) is a nonzero element of Hom_{GL_2}(τ ⊗ σ ⊗ |det|^{s−1/2}, C) for every s; take s = 1/2 and replace σ by σ^∨. Route 1 should import AL.3 rather than plan this again. Multiplicity one is not needed for Proposition 8.4.

items.name: PGSp_6, its action on ∧²F⁶ and its parabolic subgroups
items.statement: GSp_6 is the group of g ∈ GL_6 with ω(gv, gw) = ν(g)ω(v, w), where ω(e_1, e_6) = ω(e_2, e_5) = ω(e_3, e_4) = 1 and ω(e_i, e_j) = 0 for the other i < j; ν is the similitude character. P̃_1, P̃_2, P̃_3 are the stabilizers of ⟨e_1⟩, ⟨e_1, e_2⟩, ⟨e_1, e_2, e_3⟩, and P_i = P̃_i/Z(GSp_6) ⊂ PGSp_6. PGSp_6 acts faithfully on J = ∧²F⁶ ⊗ ν^{−1}; with x_ij = e_i ∧ e_j, the group of linear automorphisms of J preserving the trilinear form (x, y, z) = x ∧ y ∧ z ∈ ∧⁶F⁶ ≅ F is SL_6/μ_2, and PGSp_6 = Sp_6/μ_2 (as algebraic groups) is the stabilizer of e = x_16 + x_25 + x_34. The Levi M_3 of P_3 acts faithfully on ⟨x_12, x_13, x_23⟩, giving M_3 = GL(⟨x_12, x_13, x_23⟩) ≅ GL_3, with δ_{P_3}(m) = |det m|². P_13 = P_1 ∩ P_3 is the stabilizer of V_2 = ⟨x_12, x_13⟩, with Levi M_13 = GL(⟨x_12, x_13⟩) × GL(⟨x_23⟩) ≅ GL_2 × GL_1. P_2 is the stabilizer of the singular line ⟨x_12⟩. The standard Levi of P̃_2 is GL_2 × GL_2: α in the first factor acts on ⟨e_1, e_2⟩ in the standard way, fixes ⟨e_3, e_4⟩ and acts on ⟨e_5, e_6⟩ by the contragredient; β in the second factor acts on ⟨e_3, e_4⟩ in the standard way, on ⟨e_1, e_2⟩ by det β, and fixes ⟨e_5, e_6⟩. Hence M_2 ≅ (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇ ≅ GSO_4, with GL_1^∇ = {(t, t^{−1})}. Identify V_4 = ⟨x_13, x_23, x_14, x_24⟩ with M_2(F) by a x_14 + b x_13 + c x_24 + d x_23 ↦ (a b; c d). Then (x, x, x_56) = 2 det(x), and (α, β) acts on V_4 by x ↦ α x ᵗβ, on ⟨x_12⟩ by det(αβ) and on ⟨x_56⟩ by det(αβ)^{−1}, so M_2 acts on (V_4, det) by similitudes with multiplier det(αβ). δ_{P_2}(α, β) = |det(αβ)|⁵. M_1 ≅ GSp_4 with δ_{P_1} = |ν|³ (§13.4, p. 44).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Says M_2 acts on V_4 'preserving 2 det(x) = (x, x, x_56)'. It does not: (α, β) multiplies det(x) by det(αβ) and acts on x_56 by det(αβ)^{−1}, so the trilinear form is preserved but the quadratic form on V_4 is only preserved up to the similitude factor det(αβ), as the identification M_2 ≅ GSO_4 requires (the paper's wording has the same slip; new issue). The item also omits how the two GL_2 factors act on F⁶, the matrix identification of V_4, and that P_13 is the stabilizer of V_2 = ⟨x_12, x_13⟩. Its ν^{−1} silently corrects the paper's misprint 'J = ∧²F⁶ ⊗ i^{−1}' (new issue). items.name: Coordinates for the root system of PGSp_6
items.statement: Identify M_3 = GL(⟨x_12, x_13, x_23⟩) ≅ GL_3, so that the maximal torus is T = {(t_1, t_2, t_3)}; then t_1, t_2, t_3 (the eigencharacters on x_12, x_13, x_23) form a basis of X*(T), the root lattice. The simple coroots are α_1^∨(t) = (1, t, t^{−1}), α_2^∨(t) = (t, t^{−1}, 1) and α_3^∨(t) = (1, t, t). An unramified character is χ(t) = |t_1|^{s_1}|t_2|^{s_2}|t_3|^{s_3}. In these coordinates the simple roots are α_1 = (0, 1, −1), α_2 = (1, −1, 0) (short) and α_3 = (−1, 1, 1) (long). The simple reflections are r_1: s_2 ↔ s_3, r_2: s_1 ↔ s_2 and r_3: (s_1, s_2, s_3) ↦ (s_1 + s_2 + s_3, −s_3, −s_2). The positive coroots, in cocharacter coordinates, are e_i − e_j, e_i + e_j and (1, 1, 1) + e_i. So the root hyperplanes are s_i − s_j = 0 and s_i + s_1 + s_2 + s_3 = 0 (short roots, six) and s_i + s_j = 0 (long roots, three). χ is in the positive chamber if and only if Re s_1 > Re s_2 > |Re s_3|. The Weyl-invariant quadratic form on characters is s_1² + s_2² + s_3² + (s_1 + s_2 + s_3)² = (s_1 + s_2)² + (s_1 + s_3)² + (s_2 + s_3)², for which the Cartan matrix of (α_1, α_2, α_3) is that of C_3. The paper's form s_1² + s_2² + s_3² − ¼(s_1 + s_2 + s_3)² is the dual form on cocharacters, and there (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (0, 2, 2) are the vectors 2α^∨/q(α^∨).
items.note: Stated here with the corrected invariant form and simple roots. The paper gives q = s_1² + s_2² + s_3³ − ¼(s_1 + s_2 + s_3)² with simple roots (0, 1, −1), (1, −1, 0), (0, 2, 2), which is the invariant form and root realization on the dual (cocharacter) space (sourceIssues E9); nothing later uses it. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Keeps the paper's list of root hyperplanes, 's_i − s_j = 0 (short) and s_i + s_j = 0 (long)', which is incomplete: C_3 has 9 positive roots, and the three short-root hyperplanes s_i + s_1 + s_2 + s_3 = 0 are missing. The list is not W-stable: (s_1 − s_2)∘r_3 = s_1 + s_2 + 2s_3 (new issue). Also 'the simple reflections for α_1, α_2 permute (s_1, s_2, s_3)' should say which: r_1 swaps s_2 and s_3, and r_2 swaps s_1 and s_2. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Recomputed: r_3(s) = s − ⟨s, α_3^∨⟩α_3 forces α_3 = (−1, 1, 1). The form I + J is invariant under r_1, r_2 and r_3, and it is the standard form in the ε′-coordinates (s_1 + s_2, s_1 + s_3, s_2 + s_3). With it, B(α_1, α_2) = −1, B(α_2, α_3) = −2, B(α_1, α_3) = 0 and the norms are (2, 2, 4), giving type C_3. The corrected form and roots are right. The unrepaired hyperplane list is wrong (see statement_issue). items.name: Proposition 10.1 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_2)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(GL_2(F)) with L-parameter φ_τ and central character ω_τ, put I_2(s, τ ⊗ τ) = Ind_{P_2}^{PGSp_6}((|det|^s τ) ⊗ (|det|^s τ)) (normalized induction from M_2 = (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇). (i) If τ is unitary supercuspidal, then I_2(s, τ ⊗ τ) is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ (so ω_τ² = 1) and one of the following holds. (a) ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2; then 0 → δ_2(τ) → I_2(1/2, τ ⊗ τ) → J_2(1/2, τ ⊗ τ) → 0, with δ_2(τ) a generic discrete series. (b) ω_τ ≠ 1 (so τ is dihedral), Im(φ_τ) ≅ S_3 and s = ±1; then 0 → σ_gen[τ] → I_2(1, τ ⊗ τ) → J_2(1, τ ⊗ τ) → 0, with σ_gen[τ] a generic discrete series. (c) ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) ≇ S_3 and s = 0; then I_2(0, τ ⊗ τ) = I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_gen ⊕ I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_deg with I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_gen generic. (ii) If τ = st_χ is a twisted Steinberg representation, then I_2(s, τ ⊗ τ) is irreducible except in two cases. (a) χ = 1 and s = ±5/2 or ±1/2; then 0 → St_{PGSp_6} → I_2(5/2, st ⊗ st) → J_2(5/2, st ⊗ st) → 0 and 0 → Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6}(St)_gen → I_2(1/2, st ⊗ st) → J_2(1/2, st ⊗ st) → 0. (b) χ² = 1 ≠ χ and s = ±1/2; then 0 → σ_gen[χ] → I_2(1/2, st_χ ⊗ st_χ) → J_2(1/2, st_χ ⊗ st_χ) → 0, with σ_gen[χ] a generic discrete series.
items.note: Reducibility points computed from L-functions of Langlands parameters (Shahidi, Ann. of Math. 132 (1990)), using the local Langlands correspondence for the Levi factors. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Omits parts of the statement. In (i), second case, the paper says σ_gen[τ] is a generic discrete series; in (i), third case, that I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_gen is generic; in (ii), χ² = 1 ≠ χ, that σ_gen[χ] is a generic discrete series. The item's Ind^{PGSp_6} silently corrects the paper's misprint 'Ind^{G_2}_{P_2}' (new issue). Review note: missing is right: nothing in data/atlas.json plans p-adic PGSp_6 or G_2 representation theory, Shalika or local Fourier–Jacobi periods, or exceptional theta correspondences (searched: PGSp|GSp6|Sp6, Shalika, Fourier.Jacobi, minimal representation, exceptional theta, E7); route 1. The paper gives no proof beyond §10's pointer to Shahidi (proposed coverage item: Shahidi's reducibility theorem). Check: the Borel exponent of |det|^s st ⊗ |det|^s st is (s + 1/2, 0, −1), whose invariant norm 2s² + 3/2 equals that of ρ = (2, 1, 0), which is 14, exactly at s = 5/2. This is consistent with (ii)(a).

items.name: Proposition 10.2 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_13)
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr(GL_2(F)) with central character ω_τ, put I_13(s, τ ⊗ 1) = Ind_{P_13}^{PGSp_6}((|det|^s τ) ⊗ 1), where M_13 ≅ GL_2 × GL_1. Its restriction to Sp_6 is induced from |·|^{2s}ω_τ ⊗ |det|^s τ on GL_1 × GL_2, which is a standard module if τ is unitary tempered and s > 0. If τ is unitary supercuspidal, I_13(s, τ ⊗ 1) is reducible if and only if τ^∨ ≅ τ and one of two cases holds. (a) ω_τ = 1 and s = ±1/2; then I_13(1/2, τ ⊗ 1) has length 4 and a unique irreducible submodule δ_13(τ), which is a generic discrete series. (b) ω_τ ≠ 1, Im(φ_τ) ≇ S_3 and s = 0; then I_13(0, τ ⊗ 1) = I_13(τ ⊗ 1)_gen ⊕ I_13(τ ⊗ 1)_deg with I_13(τ ⊗ 1)_gen generic.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Omits that I_13(τ ⊗ 1)_gen is generic, and the paper's remark that for τ unitary tempered and s > 0 the restriction to Sp_6 is a standard module. The item's Ind^{PGSp_6} silently corrects the paper's misprint 'Ind^{G_2}_{P_13}' (new issue). Checked the Sp_6 restriction: (a, g) ∈ GL_1 × GL_2 ⊂ Sp_6 acts on ⟨x_12, x_13⟩ by a·g and on x_23 by det g.

items.name: Proposition 10.3 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_3; Tadić)
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(GL_3(F)) and I_3(τ) = Ind_{P_3}^{PGSp_6} τ, with M_3 ≅ GL_3. (i) If τ is a discrete series representation with trivial central character, then I_3(τ) ≅ I_3(τ^∨) is irreducible when τ ≇ τ^∨, and I_3(τ) = I_3(τ)_gen ⊕ I_3(τ)_deg with I_3(τ)_gen generic when τ ≅ τ^∨. (ii) Let χ_1, χ_2, χ_3 be characters of F^× with χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1, and let τ = τ(χ_1, χ_2, χ_3) be the associated (possibly reducible) principal series of GL_3(F). Then I_3(τ) is irreducible unless χ_i = |·|^{±1} for some i, or χ_i/χ_j = |·|^{±1} for some i ≠ j, or the χ_i are quadratic, nontrivial and pairwise different. In the last case I_3(τ) = I_3(τ)_gen ⊕ I_3(τ)_deg with I_3(τ)_gen generic.
items.note: Tadić, 'Representations of p-adic symplectic groups', Compos. Math. 90 (1994), Example 7.7 and Theorem 7.9. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Minor: omits that I_3(τ)_gen is generic, in both (i) and (ii). Review note: missing is right: nothing in data/atlas.json plans p-adic PGSp_6 or G_2 representation theory, Shalika or local Fourier–Jacobi periods, or exceptional theta correspondences (searched: PGSp|GSp6|Sp6, Shalika, Fourier.Jacobi, minimal representation, exceptional theta, E7); route 1. (ii) is consistent with the full coroot system: the coroots e_i ± e_j and (1, 1, 1) + e_i give exactly the conditions χ_i/χ_j, χ_i = |·|^{±1}, since χ_1χ_2χ_3 = 1.

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (principal series of PGSp_6 induced from P_1)
items.statement: Let τ be a supercuspidal representation of GSp_4(F) with trivial central character and L-parameter ϕ_τ : WD_F → Spin_5 ≅ Sp_4, such that std ∘ ϕ_τ contains the trivial representation (std the 5-dimensional representation). Then I_1(s, τ) = Ind_{P_1}^{PGSp_6} |ν|^s τ is reducible if and only if s = ±1/2, with 0 → δ_1(τ) → I_1(1/2, τ) → J_1(1/2, τ) → 0 and δ_1(τ) a discrete series representation.
items.note: Uses the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan–Takeda; item gsp4-llc). Review note: missing is right: nothing in data/atlas.json plans p-adic PGSp_6 or G_2 representation theory, Shalika or local Fourier–Jacobi periods, or exceptional theta correspondences (searched: PGSp|GSp6|Sp6, Shalika, Fourier.Jacobi, minimal representation, exceptional theta, E7); route 1. The statement matches the paper. Its justification is only §10's 'following Shahidi' pointer, which covers generic τ. For nongeneric supercuspidal τ, which is the case used in Proposition 15.6 (the Saito–Kurokawa τ_ρ), this is a gap; recorded as a new issue.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan–Takeda)
items.statement: (Gan–Takeda, Ann. of Math. 173 (2011), Main Theorem.) There is a surjective finite-to-one map L: Irr(GSp_4(F)) → Φ(GSp_4), π ↦ φ_π : WD_F → GSp_4(C), with the following properties. (i) π is essentially discrete series if and only if φ_π does not factor through a proper Levi subgroup of GSp_4(C). (ii) Each fibre L_φ is in bijection with the irreducible characters of A_φ = π_0(Z(Im φ)/Z_{GSp_4(C)}), which is trivial or Z/2; when it is Z/2, exactly one member is generic, the one indexed by the trivial character. (iii) sim ∘ φ_π = ω_π. (iv) φ_{π ⊗ (χ∘λ)} = φ_π ⊗ χ. (v) If π is generic or non-supercuspidal, then for every σ ∈ Irr(GL_r(F)) Shahidi's γ-, L- and ε-factors of π × σ equal those of φ_π ⊗ φ_σ. (vi) If π is non-generic supercuspidal, then for supercuspidal σ ∈ Irr(GL_r(F)) the Plancherel measure of I_{P_r}(s, π ⊠ σ) on GSpin_{2r+5} is γ(s, φ_π^∨ ⊗ φ_σ)γ(−s, φ_π ⊗ φ_σ^∨)γ(2s, Sym²φ_σ ⊗ sim φ_π^{−1})γ(−2s, Sym²φ_σ^∨ ⊗ sim φ_π). (vii) L_φ contains a generic member if and only if L(s, Ad ∘ φ) is holomorphic at s = 1. (viii) L is uniquely determined by (i), (iii), (v) and (vi) with r ≤ 2. In particular, if ω_π = 1 then φ_π takes values in Sp_4(C) ≅ Spin_5(C), and std ∘ φ_π denotes its 5-dimensional orthogonal representation.
items.note: Used to compute reducibility points for P_1 (Shahidi's method) and to state Proposition 10.4. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: 'with the properties of Gan–Takeda' is not a statement. The properties the paper uses should be stated: the parameter φ_τ, the similitude/central-character compatibility (so that trivial central character lands in Sp_4(C) ≅ Spin_5(C)), the packet structure, and the local-factor and Plancherel-measure characterization. Gan–Takeda's proof runs through theta correspondences for GSp_4 × GSO(3,3), GSO(4,0) and GSO(2,2), so MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.3 is the other candidate owner. Note: property (vi) does not cover the Levi M_1 ≅ GSp_4 of PGSp_6 (see the new Proposition 10.4 issue).

items.name: Some non-tempered representations of PGSp_6
items.statement: (a′) For τ as in (a) of item nontempered-g2, σ = τ ⊗ τ on M_2 ≅ GSO_4: I_2(σ) is a standard module with unique irreducible quotient J_2(τ ⊗ τ). (b′) For τ as in (b), σ = τ ⊗ 1 on M_13 ≅ GL_2 × GL_1: I_13(σ) is a standard module with unique irreducible quotient J_13(τ ⊗ 1). (c′) For τ as in (c), I_13(τ ⊗ 1) is a quotient of a standard module for the Borel subgroup and has a unique irreducible quotient J_13(τ ⊗ 1).
items.note: Review note: missing is right; route 1. Matches (a′)–(c′). Reviewer check: τ ⊗ τ is trivial on GL_1^∇, and I_2(τ⊗τ), I_13(τ⊗1) lie in the positive chambers of P_2 and P_13 for s > 0 (for P_13 the Sp_6 exponent is (2s′, s′, s′) with s′ = s/2 > 0). So the standard-module claims hold.

items.name: Proposition 11.1 and Corollary 11.2 (Whittaker periods; [GS04])
items.statement: Let Π be the minimal representation of E_7 and (V′, ψ′) a Whittaker datum for PGSp_6. Then Π_{V′,ψ′} ≅ ind_V^{G_2} ψ_V as G_2-modules, (V, ψ_V) a Whittaker datum for G_2. Hence (i) for generic π ∈ Irr(G_2), dim Hom_{V′}(Θ(π), ψ) = 1, so Θ(π) has a unique irreducible generic subquotient and is nonzero; (ii) for non-generic π ∈ Irr(G_2) and generic τ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6), Hom_{G_2 × PGSp_6}(Π, π ⊗ τ) = 0.
items.note: Gan–Savin 2004, Prop. 19 and Cor. 20; see also the appendix of Harris–Khare–Thorne. items.name: The Fourier–Jacobi period of G_2
items.statement: Let Q = LU be the 3-step maximal parabolic of G_2, with [L, L] ≅ SL_2 the long-root SL_2 (simple root β), so that V = U_βU is the unipotent radical of the standard Borel subgroup. The centre of U is Z(U) = U_{3α+β}U_{3α+2β}, and U/Z(U) is a Heisenberg group with centre U_{2α+β}. Put J = [L, L]U; then J/Z(U) is the Jacobi group SL_2 ⋉ U/Z(U). For a nontrivial additive character ψ, ρ_ψ is the unique irreducible representation of the double cover J̃ (pulled back from S̃L_2) that is trivial on Z(U) and on which U_{2α+β} acts by ψ; this is the Heisenberg–Weil representation. For genuine σ ∈ Irr(S̃L_2), σ ⊗ ρ_ψ is a representation of J, and the Fourier–Jacobi period of π ∈ Irr(G_2) with respect to σ is Hom_J(π, σ ⊗ ρ_ψ) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(π, Ind_J^{G_2}(σ ⊗ ρ_ψ)).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Repeats the paper's misprint 'the centre of U/[U, U] ≅ U_{2α+β}'. U/[U, U] ≅ U_α × U_{α+β} is abelian (item g2-parabolics: U_0/U_1 = U_α × U_{α+β}, U_1/U_2 = U_{2α+β}). The Heisenberg quotient is U/Z(U), with Z(U) = U_{3α+β}U_{3α+2β}, and its centre is U_{2α+β} (new issue). Review note: missing is right for the period itself. Its ingredient ρ_ψ (Stone–von Neumann plus the metaplectic extension, here for the Jacobi group S̃L_2 ⋉ H_3) is planned in MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.1, which should be cited as a prerequisite. Route 1.

items.name: Lemma 11.3 (enhanced uniqueness of the Fourier–Jacobi model)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be generic and either tempered or with cuspidal support on Q (a subquotient of Ind_Q^{G_2}σ with σ a supercuspidal representation of L). Then for every real s < 1/2, Hom_{G_2}(ind_J^{G_2}(I_ψ(−s) ⊗ ρ_ψ̄), π^∨) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(π, Ind_J^{G_2}(I_ψ̄(s) ⊗ ρ_ψ)) ≅ C, where I_ψ(s) is the genuine principal series of S̃L_2 and ρ_ψ is as in item fourier-jacobi-period.
items.note: Proof: I_ψ̄(s) ⊗ ρ_ψ ≅ ind_{T_β N}^J(|·|^{s+3/2} ψ_{2α+β}); the Whittaker functional gives a unique copy of C_c(T_γ) in π_{U,ψ_α}; temperedness controls the exponents; root exchange (Lemma 11.4) moves from T_γ N′ to T_β N. The proof is written for tempered π; for cuspidal support on Q, π_N = 0 and the same argument goes through at once. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The scope of the hypothesis should be explicit. Genericity is needed in both cases: the proof uses the multiplicity-one copy of C_c(T_γ) in π_{U,ψ_α}, which is absent for non-generic π. s is real (the proof works for Re s < 1/2). The note's supplement for cuspidal support on Q is correct: L and M are non-associate Levis (long versus short root), so by the geometric lemma π_N = 0, hence π_{V,ψ_α} = 0 and the exponent step is vacuous. Proof checked: the mirabolic step (proposed coverage item), the exponent step (δ_P^{1/2}(γ^∨(t)) = |t|³, so tempered exponents are |t|^{t+3} with t ≥ 0), the root exchange N′ = w_β N w_β^{−1}, and the conjugation of (T_βN, ψ_{2α+β}) to (T_γN′, ψ_α). The last is by w_β w_α acting on roots (β ↦ γ, 2α + β ↦ α), which the paper's 'w_α · w_β' gives under the convention X ↦ w^{−1}Xw. The proof contains misprints (new issue).

items.name: Lemma 11.4 (root exchange)
items.statement: Let H be a Heisenberg group, π a smooth H-module, X and Y maximal abelian subgroups, and ψ_X, ψ_Y characters agreeing on X ∩ Y and nontrivial on the centre of H. Then ℓ ↦ ℓ′, ℓ′(v) = ∫_{Y/X∩Y} ℓ(π(y)v) dy, is an isomorphism Hom_X(π, ψ_X) ≅ Hom_Y(π, ψ_Y).
items.note: Review note: missing; no stage plans root exchange. The proof uses Heisenberg groups and Stone–von Neumann, planned in MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.0–MP.1. Route 1.

items.name: The Shalika period of PGSp_6
items.statement: For a generic character ψ_2 of N_2 (the unipotent radical of P_2), its stabilizer in M_2 is PGL_2^Δ; the Shalika subgroup is S = PGL_2^Δ ⋉ N_2 with ψ_S extending ψ_2 trivially on PGL_2(F). The Shalika period of π is the coinvariant space π_{S,ψ_S}.
items.note: Review note: missing is right: nothing in data/atlas.json plans p-adic PGSp_6 or G_2 representation theory, Shalika or local Fourier–Jacobi periods, or exceptional theta correspondences (searched: PGSp|GSp6|Sp6, Shalika, Fourier.Jacobi, minimal representation, exceptional theta, E7); route 1. The definition agrees with Savin–Weissman §4.1 (S = Δ(GL_2) ⋉ U_3, ψ_S from ψ(−tr X) on U_3/Z_3 ≅ M_2); ψ_2 is trivial on [N_2, N_2].

items.name: Twisted Jacquet modules of the minimal representations
items.statement: (i) Let E be an étale cubic F-algebra, ψ_E a character of N in the M-orbit attached to E, and H_{J,E} = Aut(i : E → J) ⊂ H_J the stabilizer. Then (Π_J)_{N,ψ_E} ≅ ind_{H_{J,E}}^{H_J}(1) as H_J-modules (Gross–Savin, Compos. Math. 114 (1998), Lemma 2.9). (ii) For the minimal representation Π of E_7 and a Whittaker datum (V, ψ_V) of G_2, Π_{V,ψ_V} ≅ ind_S^{PGSp_6}(ψ_S) as PGSp_6-modules, where (S, ψ_S) is the Shalika subgroup and character (Savin–Weissman, Compos. Math. 147 (2011), proof of Lemma 4.5).
items.locator: (i): proof of Lemma 6.4, §6.4, p. 21; (ii): §11.3, Proposition 11.5, pp. 36–37; used in the proof of Lemma 12.1, p. 38 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: Part (i) drops its hypotheses. E is an étale cubic F-algebra (as in §6.4); ψ_E is a character of N (the Heisenberg unipotent radical of P ⊂ G_2) in the M-orbit attached to E (§3.5); and H_{J,E} = Aut(i : E → J) ⊂ H_J. For (ii), the isomorphism is in the proof of [SWe, Lemma 4.5], whose statement is about generic supercuspidal σ. items.name: The twisted Jacquet module Π_{N_2,ψ_2}
items.statement: For the minimal representation Π of E_7, Π_{N_2,ψ_2} ≅ ind_J^{G_2}(C_c(M_2°(F)) ⊗ ρ_ψ) as G_2 × PGL_2-modules, where PGL_2 acts on the trace-zero matrices M_2°(F) by conjugation, C_c(M_2°(F)) is the Weil representation of PGL_2 × S̃L_2 = SO_3 × S̃L_2, and PGL_2 acts trivially on ρ_ψ.

items.name: Lemma 11.6 (isotypic quotients of compactly induced modules)
items.statement: Let H ⊂ G and L be p-adic groups, W a smooth H × L-module and τ ∈ Irr(L) with maximal τ-isotypic quotient Θ(τ) ⊗ τ of W. If Ext¹_L(τ, τ) = 0, then ind_H^G Θ(τ) ⊗ τ is the maximal τ-isotypic quotient of ind_H^G W (compact induction).

Proof checked, including the Ext¹ step: Hom_L(W_0, τ) embeds in Ext¹_L(Θ(τ) ⊗ τ, τ) = ∏ Ext¹_L(τ, τ) = 0.

items.name: Proposition 11.7 (the Shalika period of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: As a G_2(F)-representation, Π_{S,ψ_S} ≅ (Π_{N_2,ψ_2})_{PGL_2} ≅ ind_J^{G_2}(I_ψ̄(1/2) ⊗ ρ_ψ).

items.name: Lemma 12.1 (a second chain of containments)
items.statement: Let Π be the minimal representation of E_7, π ∈ Irr(G_2) tempered, ψ_V a Whittaker character of G_2, H = PGSp_6 and τ ∈ Irr(H) tempered with Hom_{G_2 × H}(Π, π ⊠ τ) ≠ 0. Then Hom_V(π, ψ_V) ⊆ Hom_V(Θ(τ), ψ_V) ≅ Hom_S(τ^∨, ψ̄_S) ⊆ Hom_S(Θ(π^∨), ψ̄_S) ≅ Hom_{G_2}(ind_J^{G_2} I_ψ(1/2) ⊗ ρ_ψ̄, π^∨). If π is generic, all these spaces are one-dimensional.

items.name: Proposition 12.2
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6) be tempered. Then Θ(τ) cannot have two irreducible tempered generic quotients.
items.note: Savin–Weissman proved this from the uniqueness of Shalika functionals, whose proof is difficult; this proof uses only Lemma 11.3. items.name: Proposition 12.3
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and generic. Then Θ(π) cannot have two tempered irreducible quotients; in particular Θ(π)_c is irreducible or 0.

items.name: Theorem 12.4 (Howe duality for G_2 × PGSp_6, tempered case)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered with big theta lift Θ(π) on PGSp_6. (i) Θ(π) has finite length and, if nonzero, a unique irreducible quotient θ(π), which is tempered. (ii) For tempered π_1, π_2 ∈ Irr(G_2), 0 ≠ θ(π_1) ≅ θ(π_2) implies π_1 ≅ π_2.

items.name: Corollary 12.5
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be generic, supercuspidal and not a theta lift from PGL_3. Then Θ(π) is generic, supercuspidal and irreducible.
