items.name: Proposition 13.1 (r_P of the E_7 minimal representation; Magaard–Savin)
items.statement: Let H = PGSp_6 and let 𝒫 = ℳ𝒩 be the parabolic subgroup of E_7 defined by the fundamental cocharacter of P, so that 𝒫 ∩ G_2 = P, ℳ has type D_6 and 𝒩 is a Heisenberg group. Identify M ≅ GL_2 so that M acts on N/[N,N] by Sym³(std) ⊗ det^{−1}, so that a scalar (z,z) acts by z. As a GL_2 × H-module, the normalized Jacquet module r_P(Π) = δ_P^{−1/2}Π_N has a filtration with successive subquotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_P^{−1/2}·Π_𝒩 = Π_{D_6}·|det|^{1/2} ⊕ Π_∅·|det|^{3/2}, where Π_{D_6} and Π_∅ are the minimal and trivial representations of ℳ, on which the centre of M ≅ GL_2 acts trivially; (2) Ind_{B̄×P_2}^{GL_2×H}(δ·C_c(GL_1)), with B̄ the lower-triangular Borel of GL_2 acting on C_c(GL_1) by right translation by the (1,1) entry and δ(b) = |b_11|^{−1/2}|b_22|; (3) Ind_{P_13}^{H} C_c(GL_2). In (2) the action of M_2 on C_c(GL_1) and in (3) the actions of GL_2 and M_13 on C_c(GL_2) are not stated in the paper. As used in Lemma 13.4 and Theorem 14.1, M_2 acts through a character of M_2 (a power of its similitude character), GL_2 acts by translation, and M_13 ≅ GL_2 × GL_1 acts by translation through its GL_2 factor. [Magaard–Savin, Th. 6.1]
items.note: Magaard–Savin, 'Exceptional Θ-correspondences I', Compos. Math. 107 (1997), Th. 6.1. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The top piece is printed as δ_P^{−1/2}Π_N. In the paper it is δ_P^{−1/2}·Π_𝒩, with 𝒩 the unipotent radical of the E_7 parabolic 𝒫 and δ_P the modulus character of G_2. Read with N ⊂ G_2, the item makes the top quotient equal to the whole r_P(Π) = δ_P^{−1/2}Π_N. Also, the item (like the paper) leaves implicit how P_2 acts on C_c(GL_1) in (2) and how GL_2 and P_13 act on C_c(GL_2) in (3). Review note: missing is right; route 1. Reviewer check of the top piece: mapping each summand to E_7 through the fundamental cocharacter (it is ϖ_k^∨ of E_7: k = 1 for P and P_1, 3 for Q, 6 for P_2, 7 for P_3) and renormalising by δ_{𝒫}^{1/2}, the resulting cuspidal support is W(E_7)-conjugate to ρ − ϖ_4, the infinitesimal character of the E_7 minimal representation (Arthur SL_2 = subregular). This was checked by computing dominant conjugates exactly; wrong exponents fail the test. Π_{D_6}|det|^{1/2} and Π_∅|det|^{3/2} give E_7-normalized exponents −13 and −11 on ϖ_1^∨. Both pass the test and agree with Prop. 13.6(1). Also checked: (2) with δ = |·|^{−1/2}×|·| and (3) give correspondences that are functorial for G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C): I_P(τ) ↔ I_13(τ⊗1), and SO_7-parameters {ξ^{±1}|·|^{±1/2}, |·|^{±1}, 1} on both sides for (2).

items.name: Lemma 13.2 (the similitude theta correspondence for GL_2 × GSO_4)
items.statement: Let W be the Weil representation for the similitude dual pair GL_2 × GSO_4, GSO_4 ≅ (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇ acting on M_2(F) by left and right multiplication. Its irreducible quotients are π^∨ ⊗ π ⊗ π. For an irreducible generic representation π of GL_2, Θ(π^∨) = π ⊗ π and Θ(π ⊗ π) = π^∨.
items.note: Proof via W_{V,ψ} = C_c(GL_2); the Steinberg case needs Ext¹_{SO_4}(1 ⊗ 1, st ⊗ st) = 0 and the action of the centre. The similitude theta correspondence is Roberts (Israel J. Math. 94 (1996)). Review note: missing is right; route 2 (MP.3). MP.3 plans orthogonal–symplectic and unitary dual pairs, big theta modules, see-saws and Jacquet filtrations. It does not name similitude pairs such as GL_2 × GSO_4, and it excludes a full Howe duality theorem. Statement is paper-faithful. The proof's Steinberg step uses Ext¹_{SO_4}(1⊗1, st⊗st) = 0, which follows by Künneth since Hom_{PGL_2}(1, st) = 0, and uses the centre acting by scalars.

items.name: Proposition 13.3 (r_Q of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let H = PGSp_6 and let 𝒬 = ℒ𝒰 be the parabolic subgroup of E_7 defined by the fundamental cocharacter of Q (𝒬 ∩ G_2 = Q, ℒ of type A_1 × A_5). Identify L ≅ GL_2 so that L acts on U/[U,U] by the standard representation. As a GL_2 × H-module, r_Q(Π) has a filtration with successive subquotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_Q^{−1/2}·Π_𝒰 = Π_{A_5}·|det|^{3/2} ⊕ Π_{A_1}·|det|². Here Π_{A_5} is a minimal representation of the A_5 factor (a degenerate principal series induced from the stabilizer of a line, §14.3), Π_{A_1} is a principal series representation of the A_1 factor, and the centre of L acts trivially on both. (2) Ind_{B̄×P_2}^{GL_2×H}(δ·C_c(GL_1)), with δ(b) = |b_11|^{1/2}|b_22| on the lower-triangular B̄ and B̄ acting on C_c(GL_1) by right translation by b_11. (3) Ind_{P_2}^{H} W, with W the Weil representation of the similitude dual pair GL_2 × GSO_4, its first factor identified with L and GSO_4 ≅ M_2.
items.note: Its proof is 'entirely similar' to Gan–Savin 1999, Prop. 6.8 (the non-split form of H), with δ fixed by a compatibility check ('an easy exercise'). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The top piece is printed as δ_Q^{−1/2}Π_U. In the paper it is δ_Q^{−1/2}·Π_𝒰, with 𝒰 the unipotent radical of the E_7 parabolic 𝒬 (Levi of type A_1 × A_5). The item also drops the identification of L and of the first GL_2 of W. The paper leaves Π_{A_5} and Π_{A_1} unidentified (only 'the minimal and a principal series representation of the two factors of ℒ'), and it does not say how P_2 acts on C_c(GL_1). Review note: missing is right; route 1. Reviewer check of the top piece: mapping each summand to E_7 through the fundamental cocharacter (it is ϖ_k^∨ of E_7: k = 1 for P and P_1, 3 for Q, 6 for P_2, 7 for P_3) and renormalising by δ_{𝒫}^{1/2}, the resulting cuspidal support is W(E_7)-conjugate to ρ − ϖ_4, the infinitesimal character of the E_7 minimal representation (Arthur SL_2 = subregular). This was checked by computing dominant conjugates exactly; wrong exponents fail the test. The exponents −25 (Π_{A_5}) and −24 (Π_{A_1}) on ϖ_3^∨ pass the test when Π_{A_1} has infinitesimal character α (label 2) and Π_{A_5} = Ind_{P_{1,5}}^{SL_6}(|·|^{±1}). This is a reviewer identification, not the paper's. (2) and (3) are functorial (I_Q(τ) ↔ I_2(τ⊗τ); SO_7-parameters of I_Q(π(ξ^{−1}|·|^{1/2}, |·|)) and I_2(ξ∘ν) agree). The proof is only a reference to the non-split case [GS99, Prop. 6.8], with δ left as an exercise, and it prints r_{P_2}(Π) for r_Q(Π): see the new issues.

items.name: Lemma 13.4 (theta lifts of non-tempered representations of G_2)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be non-tempered. If π ⊂ I_Q(τ^∨) with τ as in (a), then Θ(π) is a quotient of I_2(τ ⊗ τ), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_2(τ ⊗ τ)) ≠ 0. If π ⊂ I_P(τ^∨) with τ as in (b) or (c), then Θ(π) is a quotient of I_13(τ ⊗ 1), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_13(τ ⊗ 1)) ≠ 0.
items.note: Uses Θ(π)^* ≅ Hom_{G_2}(Π, π), the filtration of Proposition 13.3, second adjointness, the maximal isotypic quotient of Ind_{P_2}^H W (Gan–Gurevich, Lemma 9.4) and Lemma 13.2. The second case is 'completely analogous'. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. The second bullet is 'completely analogous' and uses Proposition 13.1. There the bottom piece is Ind_{P_13}^H C_c(GL_2), so genericity of τ (which can fail in case (c)) is not needed. Checked: the Ext vanishing uses only the sign of the central exponents of (1) and the second component |·|¹ of δ in Prop. 13.3(2), against the second exponent of r_B(τ^∨), whose real part is ≤ −s/2 < 0 in case (a). The '[GG06, Lemma 9.4]' input is not covered by any item (see coverage).

items.name: Proposition 13.5 (r_{P_3} of the E_7 minimal representation; Magaard–Savin)
items.statement: Let 𝒫_3 = ℳ_3𝒩_3 be the parabolic subgroup of E_7 of type E_6 with 𝒫_3 ∩ PGSp_6 = P_3, where M_3 = GL(⟨x_12, x_13, x_23⟩) ≅ GL_3 and δ_{P_3} = |det|². Let Q_1, Q_2 ⊂ GL_3 be the block lower-triangular parabolics stabilizing the row vectors (∗,0,0) and (∗,∗,0), with Levi elements (g_1, g_2) ∈ GL_1 × GL_2 and (g_2, g_1) ∈ GL_2 × GL_1. As a G_2 × GL_3-module, r_{P_3}(Π) = δ_{P_3}^{−1/2}Π_{N_3} has a filtration with successive subquotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_{P_3}^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_3} = Π_{E_6} ⊕ Π_∅·|det|, where Π_{E_6} and Π_∅ are the minimal and trivial representations of ℳ_3 and the centre of M_3 acts trivially on both; (2) Ind_{Q×Q_1}^{G_2×GL_3}(δ·C_c(GL_1)), δ(g_1,g_2) = |g_1|^{−1/2}|det g_2|^{1/2}, with Q acting on C_c(GL_1) by left translation by det of L ≅ GL_2 and Q_1 by right translation by g_1; (3) Ind_{P×Q_2}^{G_2×GL_3}(C_c(GL_2)), with P acting by left translation via M ≅ GL_2 and Q_2 by right translation by g_2. The pieces (2) and (3) are C_c(Ω_1) and C_c(Ω_2) for the two G_2 × GL_3-orbits on the triples in O_0³ spanning a nonzero null subspace. [Magaard–Savin, §5]
items.note: Magaard–Savin 1997, §5. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The top piece is printed as δ_{P_3}^{−1/2}Π_{N_3}. In the paper it is δ_{P_3}^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_3}, with 𝒩_3 the (abelian) unipotent radical of the E_7 parabolic 𝒫_3 of type E_6. δ_{P_3}^{−1/2}Π_{N_3} is the whole of r_{P_3}(Π). The actions on C_c(GL_1) and C_c(GL_2) are not stated. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Checked: (1) passes the E_7 test (exponents −21/2 and −15/2 on ϖ_7^∨). From the displayed action ((g,m)f)(x,y,z) = |det m|²f((g^{−1}x,…)m), the modulus characters δ_{Q_1} = |g_1|^{−2}|det g_2| and δ_{Q_2} = |det g_2|^{−1}|g_1|² (both verified) and δ_{P_3} = |det|² (verified), a stabilizer computation gives exactly the stated δ in (2) and no twist in (3). (3) gives I_P(τ) ↔ I_3(Ind_{Q_2}(τ⊗1)), which has the same cuspidal data as I_13(τ⊗1).

items.name: Proposition 13.6 (r_{P_1} of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let 𝒫_1 = ℳ_1𝒩_1 be the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of E_7 (ℳ_1 of type D_6) with 𝒫_1 ∩ PGSp_6 = P_1. Identify M_1 ≅ GSp_4 so that δ_{P_1}(m) = |ν(m)|³, ν the similitude character of GSp_4. GSp_4 acts on O_0⁴ ∋ (x,y,x′,y′) by (x,y,x′,y′) ↦ (x,y,x′,y′)m^{−1}, preserving x∧x′ + y∧y′ up to scalars. Let Q_1, Q_2 ⊂ GSp_4 be the stabilizers of the row vectors (∗,0,0,0) and (∗,∗,0,0). Their Levi subgroups are L_1 ∋ (g_1,g_2) ∈ GL_1 × GL_2, acting by (x,x′,y,y′) ↦ (xg_1^{−1}, x′g_1det(g_2)^{−1}, (y,y′)g_2^{−1}), and L_2 ∋ (g_2,g_1) ∈ GL_2 × GL_1, acting by (x,y,x′,y′) ↦ ((x,y)g_2^{−1}, (x′,y′)g_1^{−1}g_2^⊤). Then ν = det g_2 on L_1 and ν = g_1 on L_2, δ_{Q_1} = |g_1|^{−4}|det g_2|² and δ_{Q_2} = |det g_2|^{−3}|g_1|³. As a G_2 × GSp_4-module, r_{P_1}(Π) = δ_{P_1}^{−1/2}Π_{N_1} has a filtration with successive subquotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_{P_1}^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_1} = Π_{D_6}·|ν|^{1/2} ⊕ Π_∅·|ν|^{3/2}, where Π_{D_6} and Π_∅ are the minimal and trivial representations of ℳ_1 and the centre of M_1 acts trivially on both; (2) Ind_{Q×Q_1}^{G_2×GSp_4}(δ·C_c(GL_1)), δ(g_1,g_2) = |g_1|^{−1/2}|det g_2|^{1/2}, with Q acting on C_c(GL_1) by left translation by det and Q_1 by right translation by g_1; (3) Ind_{P×Q_2}^{G_2×GSp_4}(C_c(GL_2)), with P acting by left translation and Q_2 by right translation by g_2. The pieces (2) and (3) come from the two G_2 × GSp_4-orbits Ω_1, Ω_2 on the nonzero quadruples spanning a null subspace with x∧x′ + y∧y′ = 0.
items.note: 'This case is not in the literature; however, it is similar to' Savin–Woodbury (J. Number Theory 146 (2015), §5). The paper describes the orbits and states the result without proof (sourceIssues E13). The text also calls ν 'the similitude character of GSp_6' where GSp_4 is meant. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The top piece is printed as δ_{P_1}^{−1/2}Π_{N_1}. In the paper it is δ_{P_1}^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_1}, with 𝒩_1 the Heisenberg radical of the E_7 parabolic 𝒫_1. The item also omits the parametrizations of the Levi subgroups L_1 ≅ GL_1 × GL_2 and L_2 ≅ GL_2 × GL_1 of Q_1, Q_2, on which δ(g_1,g_2) depends, and the normalization M_1 ≅ GSp_4 with δ_{P_1} = |ν|³. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Stated without proof (E13, confirmed). Checked: (1) passes the E_7 test (exponents −13 and −11 on ϖ_1^∨, as for Prop. 13.1). δ_{Q_1} and δ_{Q_2} were verified from the stated actions. Given the displayed exact sequence with the twist |ν(m)|³, the stabilizer computation gives exactly the stated δ in (2) and no twist in (3). The top piece is what Prop. 15.6 uses.

items.name: Proposition 13.7 (r_{P_2} of the E_7 minimal representation)
items.statement: Let 𝒫_2 = ℳ_2𝒩_2 be the parabolic subgroup of E_7 with Levi of type D_5 × A_1 and 𝒫_2 ∩ PGSp_6 = P_2, and let M_2 = (GL_2 × GL_2)/GL_1^∇ ≅ GSO_4, with the first factor acting on ⟨e_1,e_2⟩ and the second on ⟨e_3,e_4⟩. As a G_2 × M_2-module, r_{P_2}(Π) has a filtration with four successive subquotients (top to bottom): (1) δ_{P_2}^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_2} = Π_{D_5}·|det|^{1/2} ⊕ Π_{A_1}·|det|^{3/2}, with |det| = |det(αβ)|. The second SL_2 ⊂ M_2 acts trivially on the first summand and the first SL_2 on the second, and the centre of M_2 acts trivially on Π_{D_5} (the minimal representation of the D_5 factor of ℳ_2) and on Π_{A_1} (a principal series of its A_1 factor). (2) Ind_{Q×(B̄×B̄)/GL_1^∇}^{G_2×M_2}(δ·C_c(GL_1)), δ = |·|^{1/2} × |·| on each lower-triangular B̄. Q acts on C_c(GL_1) by left translation by det; B̄ × B̄ acts by right translation by the (1,1) entries, which on the product naturally means α_11β_11 (the paper does not spell this out). (3) Ind_{P×B̄}^{G_2×GL_2}(C_c(GL_2)), with B̄ in the second factor of M_2 acting on C_c(GL_2) by right translation by the scalar b_11, the first factor of M_2 acting by right translation, and P acting by left translation via M ≅ GL_2. (4) Ind_Q^{G_2} W, with W the Weil representation of GL_2 × M_2 ≅ GL_2 × GSO_4.
items.note: A combination of Gan–Savin 1999, Prop. 8.1 (the bottom piece), and the orbit analysis of the highest-weight orbit ω; the unknown twisting character δ′ is fixed by compatibility with Lemma 13.4. The notes to the proposition write M_3 for the Levi M_2 (sourceIssues E14). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The top piece is printed as δ_{P_2}^{−1/2}Π_{N_2}. In the paper it is δ_{P_2}^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_2}, with 𝒩_2 the two-step radical of the E_7 parabolic 𝒫_2 (Levi of type D_5 × A_1). The item omits: that |det| means the similitude |det(αβ)| of M_2 ≅ GSO_4; the notes to (1) (the second SL_2 is trivial on Π_{D_5}, the first on Π_{A_1}); that in (3) the first GL_2 acts on C_c(GL_2) by right translation and P by left translation; and how Q and (B̄×B̄)/GL_1^∇ act on C_c(GL_1) in (2). Review note: missing is right; route 1. Checked: (1) passes the E_7 test with |det| = |det(αβ)|: −20 for Π_{D_5}; −18 for Π_{A_1} when Π_{A_1} has infinitesimal character (3/2)α, a reviewer identification. (2) is functorial (SO_7-parameters {ξ^{±1}|·|^{±1/2}, |·|^{±1}, 1} on both sides). (3), with B̄ in the second factor, gives I_P(τ) ↔ I_2(τ ⊗ Ind(ω_τ)), whose cuspidal data equal those of I_13(τ⊗1). However, the displayed action on C_c(Ω), 'δ′(αβ)·f(ᾱg^{−1}Xβ)' with a character δ′ of M_2, cannot produce (2) and (3) for any δ′ (new issue). Also E14 (ℳ_3 for ℳ_2).

items.name: Lemma 13.8 (theta lifts of non-tempered representations of PGSp_6)
items.statement: Let σ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6) be non-tempered. Then Θ(σ) = 0 unless σ is as in Lemma 13.4. If σ ⊂ I_2(τ^∨ ⊗ τ^∨), then Θ(σ) is a quotient of I_Q(τ), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_Q(τ)) ≠ 0. If σ ⊂ I_13(τ^∨ ⊗ 1), then Θ(σ) is a quotient of I_P(τ), hence of finite length, and Θ(J_P(τ)) ≠ 0.
items.note: The proof treats standard modules for P_2, P_23 and P_12 and leaves those for P_123, P_13, P_1 and P_3 'to the reader' (sourceIssues E12). It prints J_P(τ_1) for J_P(τ_2) (sourceIssues E15). Review note: missing is right; route 1. The statement is paper-faithful. The proof covers only the first bullet (P_2), and P_23 and P_12. The second bullet and the P_123, P_13, P_1 and P_3 cases are left to the reader (E12, confirmed). E15 is confirmed. New issue: for piece (3) the proof puts B̄ in the first factor of M_2, whereas Prop. 13.7 puts it in the second. The P_2 case survives; the P_23/P_12 arguments need rearranging.

items.name: Theorem 14.1 (theta lifts of non-tempered representations)
items.statement: (a) Θ(J_Q(τ)) is a nonzero quotient of I_2(τ ⊗ τ), of finite length with unique irreducible quotient J_2(τ ⊗ τ); Θ(J_2(τ ⊗ τ)) is a nonzero quotient of I_Q(τ) with unique irreducible quotient J_Q(τ). (b) Θ(J_P(τ)) is a nonzero quotient of I_13(τ ⊗ 1) with unique irreducible quotient J_13(τ ⊗ 1); Θ(J_13(τ ⊗ 1)) is a nonzero quotient of I_P(τ) with unique irreducible quotient J_P(τ). (c) Θ(σ) = 0 for every other non-tempered σ ∈ Irr(PGSp_6). In particular, if π ⊗ σ is a quotient of Π, then π is non-tempered if and only if σ is.
items.note: The last sentence prints 'π ⊗ τ' for π ⊗ σ (sourceIssues E16). Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful (E16 corrected in the item). Implicit step: applying Lemma 13.4 to J_Q(τ) and J_P(τ), and Lemma 13.8 to J_2(τ⊗τ) and J_13(τ⊗1), needs J_Q(τ) ⊂ I_Q(τ^∨) etc. This follows from the Langlands classification, since the long Weyl element of G_2 and of C_3 is −1 (equivalently, irreducible representations of G_2 and PGSp_6 are self-dual). The second half of (b) and all of (c) rest on the omitted cases of Lemma 13.8 (E12).

items.name: Proposition 14.2 (finiteness for G_2 × SO_{2n−7} ⊂ SO_{2n})
items.statement: Let Π_n be the minimal representation of SO(2n), n = 5 or 6. For tempered π ∈ Irr(G_2), Θ_n(π) is a finite-length H_n-module, H_n = SO_{2n−7}.
items.note: Proof: Π_n is the big theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2 (Yamana, Israel J. Math. 185 (2011), Prop. 8.4, for irreducibility); a see-saw gives Θ_n(π)^* ≅ Hom_{S̃L_2}(Ω_{2n−7,ψ}, Θ̃_ψ(π)) (14.3); finiteness of Θ̃_ψ(π) for S̃L_2 × G_2 follows from Gan–Gurevich (Amer. J. Math. 128 (2006), Prop. 8.1 and Th. 9.1(c),(d)) and classical Howe duality. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. The last isomorphism of (14.3) silently identifies Θ̃_ψ̄(π)^∨ with Θ̃_ψ(π). That is harmless for finiteness, and exact when Θ̃ is irreducible, which is the case used in Lemma 15.5. The see-saw identity (14.3) deserves its own item (see coverage).

items.name: The theta correspondence for S̃L_2 × G_2 (Gan–Gurevich)
items.statement: For the dual pair S̃L_2 × G_2 ⊂ S̃L_2 × SO_7 in the Weil representation Ω_ψ: (a) Ω_N sits in 0 → Ind_Q^{G_2} C_c(GL_1) → Ω_N → C → 0 (L ≅ GL_2 acting on GL_1 through det); (b) for genuine supercuspidal σ_1 ≇ σ_2 of S̃L_2, θ̃_ψ(σ_1) ≇ θ̃_ψ(σ_2); (c) (Lemma 15.4) for each supercuspidal ρ of PGL_2, with JL(ρ) its Jacquet–Langlands transfer to PB^× = SO_3^* (B the quaternion division algebra) and σ_ρ the ψ-theta lift of JL(ρ) to S̃L_2 (an irreducible genuine supercuspidal), π_ρ := θ(σ_ρ) ∈ Irr(G_2) is nonzero irreducible supercuspidal with Θ(π_ρ) = σ_ρ; ρ ↦ π_ρ is injective on supercuspidals; and every supercuspidal π of G_2 that lifts to S̃L_2 but not to PGL_3 or PD^× is some π_ρ.
items.note: Gan–Gurevich, 'Nontempered A-packets of G_2: liftings from S̃L_2', Amer. J. Math. 128 (2006), Prop. 8.1, Lemma 9.4 and Th. 9.1. The paper's bibliography gives volume 170 and the note 'finiteness of Θ̃_ψ(π) was not formally stated there'. In (c) the paper prints 'an isotropic inner form' and 'JL(τ)' (sourceIssues E17). Review note: missing is right for the Gan–Gurevich results; route 1. The Jacquet–Langlands input JL(ρ) (PGL_2 ↔ PB^×) is planned at EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6 ('Construct local Jacquet–Langlands on essentially square-integrable representations of GL_r(D)'). The θ_ψ lift PB^× = SO_3^* → S̃L_2 is Waldspurger's classical correspondence and belongs to MP.3 (see coverage). The statement matches (a) [GG06, Prop. 8.1], (b) [GG06, Th. 9.1(c),(d)] and (c) Lemma 15.4, with E17 corrected. The bibliographic volume is 128 (E19, confirmed via Crossref).

items.name: Theorem 15.1 (Howe duality for G_2 × PGSp_6)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2). (i) Θ(π) ≠ 0 if and only if π has zero theta lift to PD^×. (ii) If Θ(π) ≠ 0, it has finite length and a unique irreducible quotient θ(π). (iii) θ(π_1) ≅ θ(π_2) ≠ 0 implies π_1 ≅ π_2. (iv) If Θ(π) ≠ 0, θ(π) is tempered if and only if π is. (v) If π is non-tempered, θ(π) ≠ 0 and its L-parameter is that of π composed with G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C).
items.note: Combines Theorem 12.4 and Theorem 14.1. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. Besides Theorems 12.4 and 14.1, (i) needs the dichotomy Theorem 6.1. (v) needs a functoriality check that the paper does not write. The reviewer checked it: I_P(τ) ↔ I_13(τ⊗1) and I_Q(τ) ↔ I_2(τ⊗τ) have matching SO_7-parameters φ ⊕ φ^∨ ⊕ det φ^{±1} ⊕ 1 and Ad φ ⊕ φ ⊕ φ^∨.

items.name: Theorem 15.2 (lifts to PGSp_6 of lifts from PGL_3)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered with π = θ_B(τ^ε) for a tempered τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3). (i) If τ ≇ τ^∨, θ(π) ≅ I_3(τ) ≅ I_3(τ^∨) ∈ Irr(PGSp_6). (ii) If τ ≅ τ^∨ and the parameter of τ contains a trivial summand, θ(π) ≅ I_3(τ). (iii) If τ ≅ τ^∨ and the parameter has no trivial summand, then π is π_gen = θ_B(τ^+) or π_deg = θ_B(τ^−), I_3(τ) = I_3(τ)_gen ⊕ I_3(τ)_deg, θ(π_gen) = I_3(τ)_gen and θ(π_deg) = I_3(τ)_deg.
items.note: The facts listed before it cite 'Theorem 15.1(v)' for the tempered case, where 15.1(ii) and (iv) are meant (sourceIssues E18). Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful; stated without proof (E22, confirmed). In (ii) the irreducibility of I_3(τ), for τ tempered and self-dual but not discrete series, with a trivial summand in its parameter, is not among Props. 10.1–10.3.

items.name: Theorem 15.3 (lifts of the remaining tempered non-supercuspidal representations)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be tempered and not a lift from PGL_3. (i) For τ a unitary discrete series representation of GL_2, I_Q(τ) is irreducible if and only if I_2(τ ⊗ τ) is; then θ(I_Q(τ)) ≅ I_2(τ ⊗ τ), and otherwise θ(I_Q(τ)_gen) ≅ I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_gen and θ(I_Q(τ)_deg) ≅ I_2(τ ⊗ τ)_deg. (ii) For τ ≅ τ^∨ supercuspidal with trivial central character, θ(δ_Q(τ)) ≅ δ_2(τ) and θ(δ_P(τ)) ≅ δ_13(τ). (iii) For τ ≅ τ^∨ supercuspidal with parameter of image S_3, θ(π_gen[τ]) ≅ σ_gen[τ]. (iv) For χ² = 1 ≠ χ, θ(π_gen[χ]) ≅ σ_gen[χ]. (v) θ(St_{G_2}) = St_{PGSp_6}.
items.note: Stated without a written proof; the paper derives the explicit lifts from four listed facts: Theorem 15.1(i), temperedness and irreducibility, non-genericity (Corollary 11.2(ii)) and cuspidal supports from §13. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful; the notation is that of Props. 3.1, 3.2, 10.1 and 10.2 (δ_Q(τ), δ_P(τ), δ_2(τ), δ_13(τ), π_gen[τ], σ_gen[τ], π_gen[χ], σ_gen[χ]). Stated without proof (E22, confirmed). Reviewer check: 'I_Q(τ) irreducible iff I_2(τ⊗τ) irreducible' does follow by comparing Props. 3.2 and 10.1 at s = 0 (supercuspidal and Steinberg cases).

items.name: The Saito–Kurokawa representations τ_ρ of SO_5
items.statement: For σ_ρ as in Lemma 15.4, τ_ρ = Θ(σ_ρ) = θ(σ_ρ) ∈ Irr(SO_5) is its ψ-theta lift from S̃L_2 to SO_5: a nongeneric supercuspidal representation of SO_5 in a Saito–Kurokawa A-packet.
items.note: Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. That τ_ρ lies in a Saito–Kurokawa packet and that std∘φ_{τ_ρ} ⊃ 1 (needed to apply Prop. 10.4 in Prop. 15.6) are asserted, not proved. A standard check: φ = φ_ρ ⊕ S_2 in Sp_4(C) gives std∘φ = 1 ⊕ φ_ρ ⊗ S_2.

items.name: Lemma 15.5
items.statement: Restrict the minimal representation of SO_12 to G_2 × SO_5. Then for ρ ∈ Irr_sc(PGL_2), Θ(π_ρ) = τ_ρ.
items.note: From the see-saw identity (14.3) and Lemma 15.4(i): Θ(π_ρ)^* ≅ Hom_{S̃L_2}(Ω_5, σ_ρ) = τ_ρ^*. Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. The proof also needs Θ(σ_ρ) = τ_ρ for S̃L_2 × SO_5 (first occurrence in the split tower, since σ_ρ comes from SO_3^*).

items.name: Proposition 15.6 (lifts of supercuspidals that do not come from PGL_3 or PD^×)
items.statement: Let π ∈ Irr(G_2) be supercuspidal and not a lift from PGL_3 or PD^×. If π = π_ρ for some ρ ∈ Irr_sc(PGL_2), then θ(π_ρ) = δ_1(τ_ρ), the square-integrable subquotient of I_1(1/2, τ_ρ) (Proposition 10.4). Otherwise θ(π) is supercuspidal.
items.note: Review note: missing is right; route 1. Paper-faithful. The proof's 'by the assumption that π does not lift to PGL_3, r_{P_i}(θ(π)) = 0 for i = 2, 3' is clear for i = 3 (top piece Π_{E_6}). For i = 2 the top piece is Π_{D_5} (G_2 × SO_3 ⊂ SO_10), and the implicit link is that the same Π_{D_5}, with the same G_2 × SO_3 ⊂ SO_10, is the top piece of the E_6 minimal representation along the D_5 parabolic attached to a maximal parabolic of PGL_3. Alternatively, it follows from (14.3) with n = 5, Lemma 15.4 and Waldspurger's dichotomy. It is terse but correct, so it is not recorded as an issue. Notation misprints are recorded as a new issue.

items.name: Corollary 15.7 (the discrete series trichotomy)
items.statement: If π ∈ Irr(G_2) is a discrete series representation which does not lift to PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z or PD^×, then θ(π) is an irreducible discrete series representation of PGSp_6. Hence every discrete series representation of G_2 lifts to a discrete series representation of exactly one of PD^×, PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp_6. That lift is Whittaker generic if and only if π is, with genericity for PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z in the sense of §8.2.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: In the corollary 'PGL_3' must be read as PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z, as in Theorem 1.3(ii). Otherwise the last sentence fails: the nongeneric discrete series π_deg = θ_B(τ^−) lifts to τ^−, whose restriction to PGL_3 is the generic τ. Review note: missing is right; route 1. No proof ('as a consequence of the explicit results'). It needs Theorems 15.2 and 15.3 and Prop. 15.6 (E22). It also needs the fact, not stated in §15, that the remaining non-supercuspidal discrete series (π_gen[1], π_deg[1], and π_gen[χ] with χ³ = 1) lift from PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z or PD^×.

items.name: Tools from smooth representation theory
items.statement: For p-adic groups and smooth representations: Frobenius reciprocity for induction and compact induction; Mackey theory for restricting induced representations; Jacquet modules and Bernstein's second adjointness; the Bernstein decomposition into cuspidal and noncuspidal parts; the Langlands classification of non-tempered irreducibles as unique quotients of standard modules; and Casselman's criterion for temperedness by the exponents of Jacquet modules.
items.note: SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Mackey filtrations and Jacquet functors; SR.2a second adjointness; SR.3 the Bernstein decomposition and the matrix-coefficient criteria for temperedness. The Langlands classification for p-adic groups is not named in SR. Review note: Status 'planned' holds only in part. SR.2 plans induction, compact induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Mackey filtrations and Jacquet functors. SR.2a plans second adjointness. SR.3 plans admissibility, the Bernstein decomposition and matrix-coefficient criteria for temperedness. No stage plans the Langlands classification (an atlas search for 'Langlands classification|Langlands quotient' finds nothing) or Casselman's exponent criterion ('Casselman' finds only AL.2's Casselman–Wallach). Split these off as a missing item routed to route 3 (see coverage), and keep this item 'planned' for the rest.

items.name: Semisimplicity of cuspidal parts and projectivity of discrete series
items.statement: For a p-adic reductive group with compact centre (G_2, PGSp_6, PGL_3, PD^×), the cuspidal component of any smooth representation is semisimple; and discrete series representations are projective in the category of tempered representations.
items.locator: §1 and proof of Proposition 5.3, pp. 4–18 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Both are used without reference: the first to give Θ(π)_c an irreducible quotient, the second for Ext¹(π_deg[1], π) = 0 with π tempered. The second is a theorem of Meyer on the tempered category. Review note: Status missing is right, and route 3 is right: SR.3 plans the Bernstein decomposition but not the semisimplicity of supercuspidal blocks for groups with anisotropic centre, and nothing plans Meyer's projectivity. The first claim holds because X^*(G)_F = 0, so each supercuspidal block contains a single irreducible that is projective and injective.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for general linear groups
items.statement: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(F), used for the Levi factors GL_2, GL_1 × GL_1 of G_2 and GL_3, GSO_4 of PGSp_6, and to attach L-parameters φ_τ to τ ∈ Irr(PGL_3).
items.note: Review note: Checked: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6 plans the characteristic-zero LLC for GL_m over p-adic fields with full Weil–Deligne parameters and the segment/Langlands-quotient theory.

items.name: Weil representations of S̃L_2 and theta lifts to O_3
items.statement: The Weil representation ρ_ψ of S̃L_2 on C_c(F) decomposes as ρ_ψ^+ ⊕ ρ_ψ^− (even and odd). For the ψ-Weil representation of O_3 × S̃L_2 on C_c(M_2°(F)) (determinant form; O_3 ≅ PGL_2 × {±1}), the big theta lifts to O_3 of ρ_ψ̄^− = (ρ_ψ^−)^∨ and ρ_ψ̄^+ = (ρ_ψ^+)^∨ are st^− and a principal series with submodule st^+ and trivial quotient; st^± is the extension of the Steinberg representation of SO_3 ≅ PGL_2 on which −1 acts by ±1. If the paper really means ρ_ψ^± as printed, the two answers may differ by the quadratic twist χ_{−1} ∘ det, which does not affect Proposition 8.4. The principal series I_ψ(s) of S̃L_2 satisfy 0 → St_ψ → I_ψ(1/2) → ρ_ψ^+ → 0 and I_ψ(1/2)^∨ ≅ I_ψ̄(−1/2), and the PGL_2-coinvariants of C_c(M_2°(F)) are the full I_ψ̄(1/2).
items.note: Classical theta for S̃L_2 × O_3 (Waldspurger), used without proof. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: In the proof of Proposition 8.4 (p. 27), the objects are defined as Θ(ρ_ψ̄^±), the lifts of the contragredients (ρ_ψ^±)^∨ = ρ_ψ̄^± via the ψ-Weil representation on C_c(M_2°(F)). The identifications are then printed for Θ(ρ_ψ^±). The item copies 'theta lift of ρ_ψ^−', which is not the object the proof uses (new misprint). Otherwise faithful. Review note: missing is right. MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.3 plans general local theta modules, see-saws and first-occurrence statements, but not the explicit (Waldspurger) S̃L_2 × O_3 correspondence. Routing it as a source of MP.3 is right only if MP.3's blueprint adds that computation.

items.name: Classical Howe duality inputs
items.statement: Howe duality (finite length of big theta lifts, and a unique irreducible quotient when nonzero) for the classical dual pairs used in §§13–15: (a) S̃L_2 × SO_{2n−7} (n = 5, 6) in the Weil representation Ω_{2n−7,ψ} (Prop. 14.2; Θ(σ_ρ) = θ(σ_ρ) = τ_ρ in §15.1); (b) the similitude pair GL_2 × GSO_4 (Roberts; §14.2 and Lemma 13.2); (c) Sp(V_6) × O(V_2′ ⊗ V_2) = Sp_6 × O_4, used through the isogeny Sp(V_2′) × Sp(V_2) → SO(V_2′ ⊗ V_2) in §14.3.
items.note: The same theorem PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 routed to MP.3 (Gan–Takeda; Waldspurger; Howe); the similitude version is Roberts. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23): statement corrected against the paper: The third 'dual pair' is misdescribed. Sp(V_2′) × Sp(V_2) → SO(V_2′ ⊗ V_2) is the isogeny. The dual pair whose Howe duality §14.3 uses is Sp(V_6) × O(V_2′ ⊗ V_2) (Sp_6 × O_4), with Θ′(σ) the big theta lift of σ ∈ Irr(Sp(V_6)) to SO(V_2′ ⊗ V_2). Review note: missing is right; route 2. MP.3 explicitly treats 'a full all-residual-characteristic Howe-duality theorem' as a separate, source-qualified extension, and it does not name similitude pairs.

items.name: The minimal representation of SO_2n as a theta lift
items.statement: The minimal representation of SO_2n (n = 5, 6) is the big theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2, and this lift is irreducible (Yamana, Israel J. Math. 185 (2011), Prop. 8.4).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 14.2, p. 50, and §14.3, first bullet, p. 51 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Review note: missing is right; route 2. Paper-faithful: the lift is along the dual pair SL_2 × O(2n), restricted to SO(2n). §14.3 uses the case n = 6 again for SO(V_2 ⊗ V_6). MP.3 does not plan minimal representations.

items.name: Whittaker-generic representations, uniqueness of Whittaker models and Rodier's heredity
items.statement: Let G be a quasi-split connected reductive group over F with Borel subgroup B = TU, and let ψ_U be a generic character of U(F), that is, trivial on [U, U] and nontrivial on each simple root subgroup. An irreducible smooth representation π of G(F) is ψ_U-generic if Hom_{U(F)}(π, ψ_U) ≠ 0. For irreducible π this space has dimension at most 1 (Gelfand–Kazhdan, Shalika). If G is adjoint (G_2, PGSp_6, PGL_3), T(F) acts transitively on generic characters, so genericity does not depend on ψ_U. (Rodier) For a standard parabolic P = MN and a finite-length smooth representation σ of M(F), dim Hom_U(Ind_P^G σ, ψ_U) = dim Hom_{U∩M}(σ, ψ_U|_{U∩M}). In particular, if σ is irreducible and generic, Ind_P^G σ has exactly one generic irreducible subquotient, occurring with multiplicity one; if σ is irreducible and not generic, Ind_P^G σ has none.
items.locator: §1, p. 3; §§3.1–3.4, pp. 9–12 (arXiv v1), used without reference
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): Genericity is used in the statements of Propositions 3.1–3.3, the tempered L-packets of §3.4, Lemma 3.4, and the generic-supercuspidal statements of §1. No item defines it, and the atlas plans Whittaker functionals only for GL_n (SR.5). Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: The Steinberg representation of a split p-adic group
items.statement: Let G be a split connected reductive group over F with Borel subgroup B. The Steinberg representation St_G is the unique irreducible subrepresentation of the normalized induction Ind_B^G(δ_B^{1/2}). Equivalently, it is the quotient of C^∞(B(F)\G(F)) by the sum of the images of C^∞(P(F)\G(F)) over the parabolic subgroups P ⊋ B. It is generic, and it is square-integrable when the centre of G is anisotropic (Casselman). For G = GL_2, st_χ = St_{GL_2} ⊗ (χ∘det).
items.locator: §3.1, Proposition 3.1(ii), p. 9 (arXiv v1), used without definition
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): St_{G_2} is used in Propositions 3.1–3.2, in the L-packet (1) of §3.4, and in the lifts of §§8 and 15 (θ(St^±)). The GL_2 Steinberg representation is planned in the GL_2 roadmaps, but no stage plans the Steinberg representation of a general split group. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Depth-zero unipotent supercuspidal representations of G_2
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G_2(F) be a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup, with reduction map K → G_2(F_q). Let G_2[1], G_2[−1], G_2[ω], G_2[ω²] be the four cuspidal unipotent representations of G_2(F_q) (Carter's G_2[1], G_2[−1], G_2[θ], G_2[θ²]). For ε ∈ {1, −1, ω, ω²}, set π_sc[ε] = c-Ind_K^{G_2(F)}(G_2[ε]), where G_2[ε] is inflated to K. Each π_sc[ε] is an irreducible depth-zero supercuspidal representation (Moy–Prasad, Morris), since G_2(F) has trivial centre. By the desiderata of §3.4, π_sc[1] is the member π(ε_{S_3}) of the packet with φ trivial, π_sc[−1] is π(−1) for φ(W_F) = μ_2 with χ unramified, and π_sc[ω], π_sc[ω²] are π(ω), π(ω²) for φ(W_F) = μ_3 with χ unramified.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): They are members of the subregular L-packets. They are used again in Proposition 7.1 (Θ(χ) = π_sc[χ], p. 23) and in §8.3 (θ(St^+) ⊕ θ(St^−) = π_gen[1] ⊕ π_sc[1], p. 25), so they lie on the way to the explicit lift tables. g2-l-packets only names them, and no atlas stage plans depth-zero or cuspidal unipotent representations. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Langlands classification and Harish-Chandra's classification of tempered representations (p-adic)
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive over F. (a) (Langlands classification: Silberger, Borel–Wallach, Konno) Every irreducible smooth representation π of G(F) is the unique irreducible quotient J(P, σ, ν) of a standard module Ind_P^G(σ ⊗ q^{⟨ν, H_M(·)⟩}). Here P = MN is a standard parabolic subgroup, σ is an irreducible tempered representation of M(F), and ν ∈ a_M^* lies in the open positive chamber for P. The triple (P, σ, ν) is determined by π up to isomorphism of σ, and π is tempered iff P = G. (b) (Harish-Chandra) Every irreducible tempered representation is a direct summand of Ind_P^G(δ) for an irreducible unitary discrete series representation δ of a Levi factor M, with (M, δ) unique up to conjugacy; Ind_P^G(δ) is a finite direct sum of irreducible tempered representations. (c) (Casselman's criterion) An irreducible π is square-integrable modulo the centre (resp. tempered) iff, for every standard parabolic P, every exponent of the Jacquet module r_P(π) has real part in the open (resp. closed) negative obtuse cone of a_M^*.
items.locator: §3.4, p. 12 (arXiv v1), used without reference; also §13.2, pp. 41–42
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): The Langlands classification is folded into smooth-rep-tools, which is marked planned, but no stage plans it. Harish-Chandra's classification of tempered representations is in no item. Both are needed to define J_P, J_Q, J_B and the partial LLC of §3.4. This item splits them off with the correct status. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Degenerate Whittaker models and the wave-front set (Mœglin–Waldspurger; Varma for p = 2)
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive over F (characteristic 0), and let π be an irreducible smooth representation of G(F) with Harish-Chandra–Howe local character expansion Θ_π = Σ_O c_O(π) μ̂_O near 1, the sum running over nilpotent orbits O. For a nilpotent Y ∈ g(F), let (N_Y, ψ_Y) be the associated degenerate Whittaker datum (for an even orbit, N_Y is the unipotent radical of the Jacobson–Morozov parabolic subgroup and ψ_Y the character defined by Y). If O ∋ Y is maximal among the orbits with c_O(π) ≠ 0, then π_{N_Y, ψ_Y} is finite-dimensional of dimension c_O(π) ≠ 0 (with suitable normalizations). If π_{N_Y, ψ_Y} ≠ 0, then O lies in the closure of an orbit O' with c_{O'}(π) ≠ 0. The wave-front set WF(π) is the set of maximal orbits with c_O(π) ≠ 0. For quasi-split G, π is generic iff WF(π) contains a regular orbit.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.4, p. 14 (arXiv v1); Mœglin–Waldspurger, Math. Z. 196 (1987); Varma, Math. Z. 277 (2014)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): This general input to Lemma 3.4, and through it to the dichotomy theorem (§6), is not planned anywhere. The lemma-3-4 note says so, but no item carries it. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Wave-front sets of nongeneric representations of G_2
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible smooth infinite-dimensional representation of G_2(F) that is not Whittaker generic. Then WF(π) consists of F-rational orbits in the subregular geometric orbit G_2(a_1). The F-rational orbits in G_2(a_1) ∩ g_2(F) are in bijection with the isomorphism classes of étale cubic F-algebras E. G_2(a_1) is even with Jacobson–Morozov parabolic P, and the orbit attached to E meets Lie(N)/Lie(Z) ≅ Sym³(F²) ⊗ det^{-1} in the binary cubic forms whose associated cubic algebra is E. The corresponding degenerate Whittaker model is π_{N,ψ_E}.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.4, p. 14 (arXiv v1); Huang–Magaard–Savin (J. reine angew. Math. 500) and Loke–Savin (Math. Ann. 340 (2008))
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the G_2-specific input to Lemma 3.4. It needs its own statement, because the lemma is used to choose E in the proof of Theorem 1.1. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Shahidi's reducibility criterion for generic supercuspidal inducing data
items.statement: Let G be a quasi-split connected reductive group over F, P = MN a maximal parabolic subgroup, α the simple root in N, α̃ = ⟨ρ_P, α^∨⟩^{−1}ρ_P, σ an irreducible unitary generic supercuspidal representation of M(F), and I(s, σ) = Ind_P^G(σ ⊗ q^{⟨sα̃, H_M(·)⟩}) (normalized). Let r_1, …, r_m be the irreducible constituents of the adjoint action of ^LM on ^Ln, and L(s, σ, r_i) Shahidi's L-functions. If w_0σ ≇ σ, then I(s, σ) is irreducible for all real s. If w_0σ ≅ σ, then at most one of L(s, σ, r_1), L(s, σ, r_2) has a pole at s = 0. If L(s, σ, r_i) has one, then for real s > 0 the induced representation I(s, σ) is reducible exactly at s = 1/i, where it has length two and its generic constituent is a discrete series subrepresentation. If neither has a pole, I(0, σ) is reducible and I(s, σ) is irreducible for s ≠ 0. For the Levis of PGSp_6 (GL_2 × GL_2/GL_1^∇, GL_2 × GL_1, GL_3, GSp_4), L(s, σ, r_i) = L(s, r_i ∘ φ_σ) under the local Langlands correspondence (Henniart for GL_n; Gan–Takeda (v) for generic representations of GSp_4).
items.locator: §10, p. 31, citing Shahidi, Ann. of Math. 132 (1990), 273–330 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): The reducibility points in Propositions 10.1, 10.2 and 10.4 are justified only by 'following Shahidi [Sh], reducibility points ... can be computed using L-functions of Langlands parameters'. No item states Shahidi's theorem, and nothing in the atlas plans Langlands–Shahidi theory (searched: Shahidi, Plancherel measure). Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Smooth representations of the mirabolic subgroup of GL_2 (Bernstein–Zelevinsky)
items.statement: Let P = {(a b; 0 1)} ⊂ GL_2(F), with U = {(1 b; 0 1)} ≅ F and T = {(a 0; 0 1)} ≅ F^×, and let ψ be a nontrivial character of U. Every smooth P-module W sits in an exact sequence 0 → C_c(T) ⊗ W_{U,ψ} → W → W_U → 0 of P-modules, where C_c(T) ≅ ind_U^P ψ (T acting by translation) and U acts trivially on W_U. Hence C_c(T) is the unique irreducible infinite-dimensional smooth P-module, and every other irreducible smooth P-module is a character of T, trivial on U.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): The proof uses the classification of smooth representations of the mirabolic subgroup T_γU_β of L ≅ GL_2 ('the mirabolic subgroup has a unique irreducible infinite-dimensional (generic) representation ... realized on C_c(T_γ)') and the exact sequence 0 → C_c(T_γ) → π_{U,ψ_α} → π_{V,ψ_α} → 0. No item covers it. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.5 plans Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives for GL_n, but over Helm's integral coefficient rings; the complex GL_2 case would be its specialization. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Savin–Weissman: lifts to PGSp_6 of generic supercuspidal representations of G_2
items.statement: Let π be a generic supercuspidal irreducible representation of G_2(F) whose theta lift to PGL_3 (dual pair PGL_3 × G_2 ⊂ E_6) is zero. Then the big theta lift Θ(π) of π to PGSp_6 (dual pair G_2 × PGSp_6 ⊂ E_7) is supercuspidal, hence a direct sum of irreducible supercuspidal representations, and exactly one of these summands is generic (Savin–Weissman, Compos. Math. 147 (2011), Propositions 3.6 and 3.7).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): The imported Savin–Weissman results are not an item; cor-12-5 only names [SWe] in its note. The precise input, read in arXiv:0908.3340v2, is Propositions 3.6 and 3.7 there. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Whittaker data and generic representations (G_2, PGSp_6)
items.statement: For a split adjoint group G (here G_2 or PGSp_6), a Whittaker datum is a pair (V, ψ_V) with V the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup and ψ_V a character of V that is nontrivial on every simple root subgroup; all Whittaker data are G(F)-conjugate. A smooth representation π of G(F) is generic if Hom_V(π, ψ_V) ≠ 0; for irreducible π this space has dimension at most 1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): Whittaker data and genericity for G_2 and PGSp_6 are used throughout §§10–12 ('generic discrete series', 'Whittaker datum for PGSp_6', 'π generic') but no item defines them. If range 1 proposes this definition for G_2 (§§3, 6), merge the two. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Parabolic subgroups of E_7 attached to the parabolics of G_2 and PGSp_6
items.statement: Let G_2 × PGSp_6 ⊂ E_7 (split, adjoint). For each maximal parabolic subgroup of G_2 or PGSp_6, the fundamental cocharacter defining it gives a Z-grading of Lie(E_7) and hence a parabolic subgroup of E_7 meeting G_2, resp. PGSp_6, in the given parabolic: P = MN ↦ 𝒫 = ℳ𝒩 (ℳ of type D_6, 𝒩 Heisenberg); Q = LU ↦ 𝒬 = ℒ𝒰 (type A_1 × A_5); P_1 ↦ 𝒫_1 (type D_6, Heisenberg); P_2 ↦ 𝒫_2 (type D_5 × A_1, 𝒩_2 two-step); P_3 ↦ 𝒫_3 (type E_6, 𝒩_3 abelian). The three 𝒫_i are the maximal parabolics containing the parabolic with Levi of type D_4 into which G_2 is embedded, and the centralizer of G_2 in E_7 is PGSp_6. In the Jacquet-module statements, Π_{D_6}, Π_{D_5} and Π_{E_6} denote the minimal representations of the corresponding Levi factors, Π_∅ the trivial representation, Π_{A_5} a degenerate principal series of the A_5 factor induced from the stabilizer of a line, and Π_{A_1} a principal series of the A_1 factor. The top piece of r_X(Π) is δ_X^{−1/2}·Π_{𝒩_X}, the coinvariants for the E_7 radical normalized by the modulus character of the small group.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): Every Jacquet-module statement in §13 is phrased through these E_7 parabolics and the representations Π_{D_6}, Π_{A_5}, Π_{A_1}, Π_{E_6}, Π_{D_5} and Π_∅ of their Levi factors. No item defines them (prop-13-1 only mentions 'Levi of type D_6'), and pgsp6-structure does not cover the E_7 side. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Null-subspace orbits and the kernels of Π_{N_i} → Π_{𝒩_i}
items.statement: (a) Nonzero subspaces of O_0 on which octonion multiplication vanishes have dimension 1 or 2, and G_2 acts transitively on those of each dimension (stabilizers Q and P). (b) (P_3) With Ω ⊂ O_0³ the triples spanning a nonzero null subspace, there is an exact sequence of G_2 × GL_3-modules 0 → C_c(Ω) → Π_{N_3} → Π_{𝒩_3} → 0 with ((g,m)f)(x,y,z) = |det m|² f((g^{−1}x, g^{−1}y, g^{−1}z)m). G_2 × GL_3 has two orbits Ω_1, Ω_2 (span of dimension 1, 2), so C_c(Ω) contains C_c(Ω_2) with quotient C_c(Ω_1). (c) (P_1) With Ω ⊂ O_0⁴ the nonzero quadruples spanning a null subspace and satisfying x∧x′ + y∧y′ = 0, there is an exact sequence of G_2 × GSp_4-modules 0 → C_c(Ω) → Π_{N_1} → Π_{𝒩_1} → 0 with ((g,m)f)(x,y,x′,y′) = |ν(m)|³ f((g^{−1}x, …, g^{−1}y′)m), again with two orbits Ω_1, Ω_2. (d) (P_2) With ω the ℳ_2-highest-weight orbit in 𝒩̄_2/𝒵̄_2 ≅ M_2(O) (nonzero matrices whose columns are F-linearly dependent highest-weight vectors of the half-spin module) and Ω ⊂ ω the matrices with traceless entries, there are exact sequences 0 → C_c(ω) → Π_{𝒵_2} → Π_{𝒩_2} → 0 and 0 → C_c(Ω) → (Π_{𝒵_2})_{N_2} → Π_{𝒩_2} → 0, with G_2 × M_2 acting through X ↦ ᾱg^{−1}Xβ and a twist, and two orbits Ω_1, Ω_2 by the dimension of the span of the entries.
items.locator: §13.4, Cases P_3, P_1 and P_2, pp. 43–46 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): These exact sequences, with the stated twisted actions, are the actual input from which (2) and (3) of Propositions 13.5–13.7 are read off. They are the part of Case P_1 that is unproved (E13), and for P_2 the displayed action is inconsistent with the stated result (new issue). A formaliser needs them as separate statements. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Isotypic quotients of Ind_{P_2}^{PGSp_6} W (Gan–Gurevich, Lemma 9.4)
items.statement: Let W be the Weil representation of the similitude dual pair GL_2 × GSO_4, with GSO_4 ≅ M_2 the Levi factor of P_2 ⊂ PGSp_6, and let τ ∈ Irr(GL_2). As a GL_2 × PGSp_6-module, the maximal τ-isotypic quotient of Ind_{P_2}^{PGSp_6} W is (Ind_{P_2}^{PGSp_6} Θ_W(τ)) ⊗ τ, where Θ_W(τ) is the big similitude theta lift of τ to GSO_4.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 13.4, p. 43 (arXiv v1), citing Gan–Gurevich, Amer. J. Math. 128 (2006), Lemma 9.4
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): Used to identify the maximal τ^∨-isotypic quotient of the bottom piece of Proposition 13.3. The paper's own Lemma 11.6 (item lemma-11-6) does not cover it: its hypothesis Ext¹_L(τ,τ) = 0 fails for L = GL_2, whose centre is noncompact. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Isotypic quotients of the regular representation
items.statement: Let G be a p-adic reductive group and σ an irreducible admissible representation of G. The maximal σ-isotypic quotient of C_c^∞(G) (right translation, with G × G acting by left and right translation) is σ^∨ ⊗ σ.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 13.2, p. 41; proof of Lemma 13.8, p. 48; §14.2, p. 49 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): A basic fact used four times in the range, with no item. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: The see-saw identity (14.3)
items.statement: Let n ∈ {5, 6}. Let Π_n, the minimal representation of SO_{2n}, be realized as the big theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2, and let G_2 × SO_{2n−7} ⊂ SO_7 × SO_{2n−7} ⊂ SO_{2n}. For π ∈ Irr(G_2), as SO_{2n−7}-modules, Θ_n(π)^* = Hom_{G_2}(Π_n, π) ≅ Hom_{SL_2}(Ω_{2n−7,ψ} ⊗ Θ̃_ψ̄(π), C) ≅ Hom_{S̃L_2}(Ω_{2n−7,ψ}, Θ̃_ψ(π)). Here Ω_{2n−7,ψ} is the Weil representation of S̃L_2 × SO_{2n−7} and Θ̃_ψ(π) is the big ψ-theta lift of π to S̃L_2 via the Weil representation of S̃L_2 × SO_7 ⊃ S̃L_2 × G_2. (The last isomorphism identifies Θ̃_ψ̄(π)^∨ with Θ̃_ψ(π); it holds exactly when Θ̃ is irreducible, and up to finite length otherwise.)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): A displayed, numbered identity, reused in Lemma 15.5 and Proposition 15.6. Item prop-14-2 mentions it only in its note, and item seesaw is a different see-saw ((4.1)/(5.1)). Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Finiteness for Sp(V_6) × Sp(V_2) in the minimal representation of SO(V_2 ⊗ V_6)
items.statement: Let V_2, V_2′ and V_6 be symplectic spaces of dimensions 2, 2 and 6, and let Π_6 be the minimal representation of SO(V_2 ⊗ V_6), realized as the big theta lift of the trivial representation of Sp(V_2′) through the Weil representation Ω of Sp(V_2′) × SO(V_2 ⊗ V_6). For σ ∈ Irr(Sp(V_6)), Θ(σ)^* ≅ Hom_{Sp(V_6)}(Π_6, σ) ≅ Hom_{Sp(V_2′)×Sp(V_6)}(Ω, 1 ⊗ σ) ≅ Hom(Θ′(σ), 1_{Sp(V_2′)}), where Θ′(σ) is the big theta lift of σ to SO(V_2′ ⊗ V_2), whose image of the isogeny Sp(V_2′) × Sp(V_2) → SO(V_2′ ⊗ V_2) has finite index. Hence Θ(σ) has finite length as an Sp(V_2)-module.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the argument for the top piece of Prop. 13.1 in the finiteness of Θ(σ)_nc, i.e. Lemma 6.2(ii) for PGSp_6. It is purely classical, so it belongs with MP.3. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.

items.name: Restriction of Π_{A_5} to Sp_6
items.statement: Let Π_{A_5} = Ind_{P_{1,5}}^{SL_6}(χ) be a degenerate principal series of SL_6 induced from the stabilizer of a line in F⁶. Since Sp_6 acts transitively on the lines, the restriction of Π_{A_5} to Sp_6 ⊂ SL_6 is the degenerate principal series of Sp_6 induced from the stabilizer of a line. Consequently, for σ ∈ Irr(Sp_6), the multiplicity space Hom_{Sp_6}(Π_{A_5}, σ)^∨ has finite length.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the argument for the top piece of Prop. 13.3 in the finiteness of Θ(σ)_nc (Lemma 6.2(ii) for PGSp_6). It is short but a distinct fact. Route: ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2.

items.name: Finite length of the noncuspidal part via Jacquet modules
items.statement: Let V be a smooth representation of a p-adic reductive group G with trivial cuspidal component (V = V_nc). If the Jacquet module r_P(V) has finite length for every maximal proper parabolic subgroup P, then V has finite length.
items.locator: §14.2, p. 49, and proof of Proposition 14.2, p. 51 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): Every finiteness argument in §14 reduces to this criterion. Route: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

items.name: Local Jacquet–Langlands for PGL_2 and PB^×
items.statement: Let B be the quaternion division algebra over F. There is a bijection ρ ↦ JL(ρ) from the discrete series representations of PGL_2(F) to the irreducible representations of PB^× = SO_3^*, characterized by the character identity on regular elliptic elements (with sign −1). In particular it is defined on the supercuspidal representations of PGL_2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): It is used to define σ_ρ, π_ρ and τ_ρ, and no item covers it. It is planned by ET.6 (local Jacquet–Langlands for GL_r(D)); the new roadmap imports it from there.

items.name: Theta lifts from SO_3^* = PB^× to S̃L_2 (Waldspurger)
items.statement: For ρ a supercuspidal representation of PGL_2(F), the ψ-theta lift σ_ρ of JL(ρ) ∈ Irr(PB^×) = Irr(SO_3^*) to S̃L_2(F) is nonzero, irreducible, genuine and supercuspidal, and its ψ-theta lift to the split SO_3 vanishes (Waldspurger's dichotomy).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (coverage of the paper): It defines σ_ρ, 'an irreducible supercuspidal genuine representation of S̃L_2'. This is Waldspurger's classical correspondence for S̃L_2 × O_3^*, and no item covers it: sl2-o3-theta treats the split O_3 only. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.

routes.title: Exceptional theta correspondences for G_2: minimal representations, Howe duality and theta dichotomy
routes.brief:
A new roadmap for the exceptional theta correspondences of Gan–Savin, 'Howe duality and dichotomy for exceptional theta correspondences' (Invent. Math. 232 (2023); arXiv:2102.00372). The roadmap covers the restriction of minimal representations of adjoint groups of type E to the dual pairs PD^× × G_2 ⊂ E_6^D, (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 ⊂ E_6 ⋊ Z/2Z and G_2 × PGSp_6 ⊂ E_7 over a p-adic field F of characteristic 0 (D a cubic division algebra). Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.1 (dichotomy): every π ∈ Irr(G_2(F)) has nonzero theta lift to exactly one of PD^× and PGSp_6(F). Theorem 1.2 (Howe duality): for π_1, π_2 ∈ Irr(G_2(F)), Θ(π_i) has finite length and dim Hom_{H_J}(θ(π_1), θ(π_2)) ≤ dim Hom_{G_2}(π_1, π_2); for τ ∈ Irr(H_J), Θ(τ) has finite length with a unique irreducible quotient if nonzero. There are injections θ_D : Irr^♥(PD^×) ↪ Irr(G_2) (with Irr^♥(PD^×) = Irr(PD^×) if p ≠ 3), θ_B : Irr^♥(PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) ↪ Irr(G_2) with image disjoint from that of θ_D, and θ : Irr(G_2) ∖ Im θ_D ↪ Irr(PGSp_6). Theorem 1.3: the correspondences preserve temperedness; every discrete series of G_2 lifts to a discrete series of exactly one of PD^×, PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp_6; and they are functorial on non-tempered representations. The explicit lifts of Theorems 8.2, 8.5, 14.1, 15.1–15.3, Proposition 15.6 and Corollary 15.7 are also final results. Cover, in this order: (1) the split octonions (import Tau Ceti's Octonion) and G_2 = Aut(O), identified with the split Chevalley group of type G_2, with its parabolic subgroups P and Q, SL_3 ⊂ G_2 and the needed facts about G_2(C); (2) representations of p-adic G_2: Muić's reducibility results (Propositions 3.1–3.3), the Langlands classification of the non-tempered representations, the partial local Langlands correspondence of §3.4, and degenerate Whittaker models along N indexed by cubic algebras (Mœglin–Waldspurger, Varma; Lemma 3.4); (3) Freudenthal–Jordan algebras of dimension 1, 3, 9 and 15, the Lie algebras g_J and groups G_J (including E_6^D and Spin_8^E), the dual pairs G_2 × Aut(J) and Aut(i : E → J) × Spin_8^E, and the see-saw; (4) minimal representations Π_J and big theta lifts, with the twisted Jacquet modules the proofs use and the Jacquet-module filtrations of §13 (Magaard–Savin, Gross–Savin, Savin, Gan–Savin, Savin–Weissman); (5) the degenerate principal series I_E(s) of Spin_8^E, the representations R_J(E), the Mackey filtration of I_E(s) restricted to G_2, and the Ext vanishing of §5; (6) the dichotomy theorem (§6); (7) PD^× × G_2 (§7, with Savin's results and Lonka–Tandon); (8) (PGL_3 ⋊ Z/2Z) × G_2 (§8, with Gan–Savin 2004); (9) the representations of PGSp_6 that are needed (§§9–10, principal series from P_1, P_2, P_3 and P_13, after Tadić and Gan–Takeda) and the Fourier–Jacobi and Shalika periods and root exchange of §11; (10) Howe duality for G_2 × PGSp_6 (§§12–15), with the auxiliary pairs G_2 × SO_{2n−7} ⊂ SO_{2n} and S̃L_2 × G_2 (Gan–Gurevich). Treat the steps the paper leaves open (sourceIssues E10, E12, E13 and E20–E22) as proof obligations. They are: Proposition 5.4; Lemmas 8.1 and 8.3; the computation of Π_{N_2,ψ_2}; Proposition 13.6; the cases left to the reader in Lemma 13.8 and §14.3; and the explicit lifts of Theorems 15.2–15.3. The published version, which was not accessible, may supply some of them. Design the roadmap so that PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B, the local Langlands correspondence for G_2 built on this paper, can extend it. Import from: Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.2, SR.2a and SR.3. Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms) MP.2–MP.3, for classical Weil representations and classical Howe duality; this extraction routes those inputs to MP.3. Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4, for the local Langlands correspondences of classical groups (GSp_4, Sp_6). Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.6, for GL_n and the inner form PD^×. Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight) Layer 8, for the split octonions and the exceptional Lie algebras. Clifford algebras, the Pin and Spin groups, and spin representations (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SpinRepresentations) Layer 8, for triality. Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) Layer 9, for the split Chevalley groups of types G_2, E_6 and E_7.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23, against arXiv v1; the published version is closed access), to respect when stating the layers:
- Several steps of arXiv v1 are stated without proof, and the main theorems' proofs rest on them. Plan each as a layer obligation. Proposition 5.4 (the Mackey decomposition of I_E(s)|_{G_2}; E20) carries the dichotomy and §§6–8. The twisted Jacquet module of §11.4 (E10) carries tempered Howe duality for generic tempered π. The P_1 case of the Jacquet-module computation (Proposition 13.6; E13), the omitted cases of Lemma 13.8 (E12), Theorems 15.2–15.3 (E22), the Z/2Z refinement in Lemma 8.1 and Lemma 8.3 (E21), and the split case of Proposition 13.3 remain.
- Proposition 10.4 cites Shahidi, which covers generic supercuspidals only, but §15 applies it to the non-generic Saito–Kurokawa τ_ρ. Prove that case, for instance through Plancherel measures of the L-packet.
- Theorem 8.2(i) and the 'if' direction of Theorem 8.5(iii) ('τ generic ⇒ θ(τ^+) generic') fail for nontempered generic τ whose G_2 standard module is reducible, e.g. τ = Ind(|·| ⊗ μ ⊗ |·|^{−1}μ^{−1}). Restrict them to tempered τ. §8.1 also omits the trivial representation of PGL_3 among the nongeneric self-dual ones.
- In Propositions 3.1(iii) and 3.2(iii), the quotients are J_Q(1, ·), not J_Q(1/2, ·). §9's root hyperplanes are incomplete (6 of 9). In the Jacquet-module statements of §13, the top pieces are coinvariants for the E_7 radical 𝒩_i, not N_i.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas plans exceptional groups over p-adic fields, minimal representations or exceptional dual pairs, and nothing plans the representation theory of p-adic G_2. The nearest roadmaps plan classical theta correspondences for the Weil representation (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms), smooth representation theory in general (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups), and the split octonions and exceptional Lie algebras over a characteristic-0 field (Tau Ceti's LieHighestWeight, Layer 8). None goes in this direction, so a Part II of any of them would stretch its scope. The roadmap imports those roadmaps and is designed for its only queued consumer, the local Langlands correspondence for G_2 (PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B).

The paper also uses classical theta correspondences, which MP.3 owns: the Weil representations of S̃L_2 and their lifts to O_3, Howe duality for classical and similitude dual pairs, the similitude correspondence for GL_2 × GSO_4 (Lemma 13.2, proved in the paper), and the minimal representation of SO_2n as the theta lift of the trivial representation of SL_2. PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 routed classical Howe duality to MP.3 as well.

Two facts about the category of smooth representations are used without reference. For groups with compact centre, cuspidal parts are semisimple; and discrete series are projective in the tempered category. Both concern the Bernstein decomposition and temperedness, which SR.3 plans.
The local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan–Takeda) is a classification input for a classical similitude group, the kind of input ML.4 owns. Here it computes reducibility points for P_1.

sourceIssues.printed: “Consider i = 3. sourceIssues.correction: With B̄ in the second factor, as in Prop. 13.7: Ext^i_{M_2}(piece (3), τ_1^∨ ⊗ τ_2^∨) ≅ Ext^i_{GL_2×T}(Ind_P^{G_2}(C_c(GL_2)), τ_1^∨ ⊗ r_B(τ_2^∨)). The P_2 case goes through unchanged, since τ_2 is also a positive twist of a tempered representation. In the P_23 case the i = 3 term should still vanish, but by a different reason: τ_2 is now the principal-series factor, and its exponent on the second GL_1 is nonzero because s_1 > s_2 > 0. In the P_12 case the i = 3 term can be nonzero (e.g. τ_2 a Steinberg twist by |det|^{1/2}), so the paper's P_12 argument must be rerun with τ_1 and τ_2 exchanged: Θ(σ) is then a quotient of I_P(τ_1), followed by Lemma 13.4. The conclusion Θ(σ) = 0 is not affected.
sourceIssues.reason: Three facts put B̄ in the second factor, against the Lemma 13.8 proof. First, the Ω-model: the A_1 factor of ℳ_2, i.e. the second SL_2, since (1)'s notes make the first SL_2 lie in D_5, acts on M_2(O) from the right, and the stabilizer of a point of Ω_2 contains a Borel of the right-acting factor. Second, the functoriality check: I_13(τ⊗1) has P_2-cuspidal data with τ on the first factor (GL_2 on ⟨e_1,e_2⟩) and ω_τ on e_3, which is what (3) with B̄ in the second factor produces. Third, with B̄ in the first factor, (3) would pair I_P(τ) with τ on GSp_2, whose SO_7-parameter Ad φ_τ ⊕ … does not match. The proof of Lemma 13.8 applies second adjointness in the first factor throughout, so its i = 3 steps for P_23 and P_12 are argued for the wrong factor.

sourceIssues.reason: Reviewer computation. Take the point X_0 of Ω_2 with first column (v_1; v_2), a basis of the null plane V_2, and second column 0. Its stabilizer is S = {(g,[α,β]) : g ∈ P, β ∈ B̄, ᾱ = β_11^{−1}ℓ(g)^⊤}, where ℓ(g) is the matrix of g on V_2; ᾱ may be read as transpose or as adjugate. On S, det α·det β = det ℓ(g)·β_22/β_11. Every character of M_2 is a power of det α·det β. So the displayed action gives C_c(Ω_2) ≅ c-ind_S(|det ℓ|^e|β_22/β_11|^e). The untwisted (3) is c-ind_S(δ_R^{1/2}|_S) = c-ind_S(|det ℓ|^{3/2}|β_22/β_11|^{1/2}), with R = P × (GL_2×B̄)/GL_1^∇, which needs e = 3/2 and e = 1/2 at once. Similarly on the stabilizer of v ⊗ E_11 in Ω_1 (g ∈ Q, α, β ∈ B̄, α_11β_11 = det ℓ), the stated (2) gives |det ℓ|^{5/2}|α_22β_22|^{3/2}, while the display gives |det ℓ|^e|α_22β_22|^e. Conversely (3) as stated gives I_P(τ) ↔ I_2(τ ⊗ Ind(ω_τ)), which has the cuspidal data of I_13(τ⊗1) (Lemma 13.4). And (2) gives SO_7-parameters {ξ^{±1}|·|^{±1/2}, |·|^{±1}, 1} on both sides, as G_2(C) ⊂ Spin_7(C) requires. So the derivation offered for (2) and (3) fails, while the statements survive.
